records.title: Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation

postedPay.title: Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation

records.description:
Why Hershey:

At The Hershey Company, our culture is rooted in purpose and inspired by Milton Hershey’s enduring vision that business should create opportunity for others. Through our commitment to corporate philanthropy, we create positive impact by supporting communities, helping children thrive, and operating as a business for good. This includes our deep and long standing partnership with Milton Hershey School, where we invest in education, workforce readiness, and hands on engagement to help students succeed beyond the classroom. Supported by strategic grantmaking, product donations, cross brand collaboration, and strong employee volunteerism, Hershey offers a place to work where making a difference—locally and globally—is part of how we do business every day.

 

Location: This role is based in Hershey, PA with an expectation of 3 days in office per week.

**About the Hershey Company**
-----------------------------

At The Hershey Company, we make more moments of goodness through some of the world's most iconic brands, including Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat®, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Dot's Pretzels, Lesser Evil and more. Our team supports a global portfolio of over 90 brands, creating opportunities to shape strategies and drive impact across a breadth of businesses that few companies can offer. While many organizations focus on a handful of brands, Hershey provides exposure to a diverse portfolio of category-leading brands enjoyed by consumers around the world. What truly sets us apart is our legacy. Inspired by Milton Hershey's belief that business should create opportunities for others, we have been making a positive impact for more than a century through our commitment to communities, philanthropy, and our longstanding partnership with Milton Hershey School. When you join Hershey, you become part of a company where purpose, growth, and making a difference are woven into how we do business every day.

**How will you fit in the big picture?**
----------------------------------------

The Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation serves as the enterprise owner of the Hershey Lean Production System, or HLPS, and leads the continued evolution of Lean manufacturing across Hershey’s global manufacturing network.

 

This leader defines strategy, governance, standards, maturity model, deployment approach and capability requirements for HLPS. The Director partners with plant and functional leaders to eliminate systemic losses, strengthen operator ownership and accelerate manufacturing transformation through digital Lean, connected-worker solutions, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacity optimization.

 

The role ensures a consistent enterprise operating system while enabling each site to deploy HLPS according to its business needs, maturity and performance priorities.

**What will you do?**
---------------------

* **Own HLPS strategy and governance:** Define and maintain the HLPS architecture, principles, pillar standards, maturity model, assessment methodology, deployment roadmap and governance routines. Set the multi-year strategy and annual priorities, benchmark externally and translate proven practices into enterprise standards.
* **Lead network deployment:** Partner with Plant Managers to establish site transformation roadmaps, conduct quarterly progress reviews, address enterprise barriers, require recovery plans for material gaps and accelerate the replication of successful practices.
* **Build Lean leadership capability:** Establish role-based capability expectations, learning pathways, qualifications and coaching models for plants, Operational Excellence, engineering and frontline leaders. Build internal coaches and assessors while strengthening Daily Management, Leader Standard Work, structured problem solving, Autonomous Maintenance and Focused Improvement.
* **Advance manufacturing transformation:** Lead strategy and governance for assigned initiatives in digital Lean, connected worker, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacityoptimization. Establish prioritization, pilot criteria, stage gates, value-realization requirements and scalable deployment standards in partnership with Engineering, Supply Chain Strategy, Digital/IT and Finance.
* **Deliver measurable business value:** Translate operational losses and capability gaps into an enterprise improvement portfolio. Connect HLPS maturity to safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, productivity and people outcomes, partnering with Finance to validate benefits.
* **Lead and develop the team:** Guide Lean Program Leads and transformation and technical resources, focusing support on the network’s highest-value opportunities.

**Minimum Education & Requirements**
------------------------------------

**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, business or related discipline.
* Master’s degree preferred.

 

**Experience:**

* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, engineering or Operational Excellence, including 5+ years leading leaders, multi-site programs or enterprise-scale manufacturing transformation.
* Demonstrated success designing, deploying or materially advancing Lean, Total Productive Maintenance, or a manufacturing operating system across multiple sites.
* Strong knowledge of Lean management systems, TPM, Daily Management, structured problem solving, loss analysis, asset reliability and capability development.
* Proven ability to influence Plant Managers and senior cross-functional stakeholders without relying on direct authority.
* Strong executive communication, coaching and change-leadership skills.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent demonstrated experience preferred.
* Experience in automated or capital-intensive manufacturing is strongly preferred.
* Previous leadership of a manufacturing site, major production operation or enterprise or multi-site Operational Excellence transformation strongly preferred.
* Consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, or other regulated manufacturing experience preferred.

**Benefits and Perks**
----------------------

At Hershey, we offer competitive pay and a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, financial security, and life outside of work.

* Health & Wellbeing: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus wellness programs that support your physical and mental health begin on Day 1.
* Financial Security: Competitive pay, annual incentive opportunities, and a 401(k) with company match
* Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off, company holidays, and flexible ways of working where applicable
* Growth & Development: Career development programs, learning opportunities, and internal mobility

 

*Benefits may vary based on role, location, and eligibility.*

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $166,400 to $208,000 per year. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of job‑related factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skill set, education, and training. In addition to a market-competitive base salary, our Total Rewards package includes performance‑based incentives and a comprehensive, competitive benefits package designed to support overall physical, mental, and financial well‑being (as applicable). Learn more about Hershey’s benefits and all the resources Hershey provides to support our employees’ physical, emotional, and financial well‑being by visiting the Hershey Digital Employee Experience at www.askHRbenefits.hersheys.com

The Hershey Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The policy of The Hershey Company is to extend opportunities to qualified applicants and employees on an equal basis regardless of an individual's race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, citizenship status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, transgender status, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other categories protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. 
 
The Hershey Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer - Minority/Female/Disabled/Protected Veterans. You may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access our online application process as a result of a disability. 
You can request an accommodation via phone or email.To request an accommodation via phone, please call +1 877-804-1794 and leave a voicemail with your contact information. You may also email a request for accommodation to ApplicationHelp@hersheys.com. Please be sure to include “Accommodation Needed” in the subject line. This will ensure that your email is routed to the appropriate contact who will handle your request.

records.title: Director of Operations (PCNY - Queens)
records.description:
**ABOUT US:** 
With a dedication to our people and our products, The Honickman Companies® are collectively one of the largest independent beverage employers in the country. Our Pepsi business includes distribution for brands like Pepsi-Cola, Starbucks, Lipton Teas, Gatorade, Evian and more, throughout the 5 Borough’s, Long Island, Westchester and Pennsauken NJ. If you are excited to work with some of the biggest brands in the world, in the biggest brand market in the world, come see what we have to offer. a passionate, self-motivated, and detail-oriented team player who is committed to the success of our customers. You will focus on growing and developing existing clients, as well as generating new business by identifying, implementing and executing new strategies.
 
 
**SUMMARY:** 
Leads the day-to-day operations of a large-scale beverage manufacturing facility, with overall accountability for Production, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Receiving and Warehousing. Establishes operating priorities and develops leaders and teams to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective and efficient production. Applies practical business judgment, disciplined execution and continuous improvement through the Honickman Management Operating System to improve plant performance and support the Company’s business strategy.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 

* Provides visible, hands-on leadership and direction for all plant operations, including Production, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Receiving and Warehousing.
* Establishes clear operating priorities, performance expectations and accountability; aligns staffing, resources and production plans with customer and business requirements.
* Ensures production schedules are achieved while meeting safety, food safety, quality, efficiency, cost and customer service expectations.
* Monitors and acts upon key performance indicators, including safety performance, schedule attainment, production efficiency, equipment utilization, downtime, waste, labor productivity, inventory accuracy and service levels.
* Identifies operating constraints and performance gaps; leads root cause analysis, corrective actions and practical solutions that improve throughput, reliability and execution.
* Ensures manufacturing processes, standard operating procedures and controls are documented, consistently followed and improved as business needs evolve.
* Partners with Quality leadership to maintain effective food safety, sanitation, preventive control and quality systems and to resolve customer complaints, audit findings and corrective actions promptly.
* Provides leadership and oversight for preventive and predictive maintenance, work-order execution and equipment reliability; aligns maintenance priorities with production requirements and long-term asset needs.
* Supports capital planning and execution, including equipment upgrades, facility improvements and other investments that improve safety, capacity, reliability or cost performance.
* Oversees warehouse, inventory control, shipping and receiving operations to ensure accurate inventory, efficient material flow, appropriate space utilization and timely customer shipments.
* Drives practical, results-oriented continuous improvement through the Honickman Management Operating System; ensures initiatives produce measurable gains in safety, quality, productivity, waste, cost and equipment effectiveness.
* Develops and manages operating plans and budgets; controls labor, overtime, waste, operating expense and other key financial measures while balancing service and production needs.
* Leads, develops and holds department managers and supervisors accountable; builds leadership capability, cross-functional collaboration and a strong succession pipeline.
* Builds a culture of teamwork, communication, employee engagement and ownership by maintaining a regular presence on the plant floor and engaging employees at all levels.
* Establishes productive relationships with employees and union representatives; ensures consistent application of Company policies, procedures and applicable collective bargaining agreements and addresses employee relations matters promptly and professionally.
* Promotes a proactive safety culture and ensures compliance with applicable OSHA, environmental, food safety, regulatory and customer requirements; directs timely incident investigations and corrective actions.
* Provides accurate and timely operating reports, communicates plant performance and risks, and recommends actions needed to achieve business objectives.
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:** 
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 

* Comprehensive knowledge of large-scale manufacturing operations, production planning, equipment reliability, quality systems, food safety, warehousing, distribution and inventory controls.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to develop operating plans, manage budgets and labor costs, interpret performance data and translate findings into action.
* Practical knowledge of continuous improvement, root cause analysis, standard work and performance management; ability to implement solutions that deliver measurable operational results.
* Demonstrated ability to lead a complex operation through multiple levels of management and to establish priorities, accountability and disciplined execution across functions.
* Working knowledge of OSHA, environmental and food-manufacturing regulatory requirements and the ability to maintain effective safety, quality and compliance systems.
* Proven ability to lead and develop managers and supervisors, engage a diverse hourly workforce and build effective labor-management relationships in a union environment.
* Excellent judgment, problem-solving, organizational and follow-up skills; able to manage competing priorities and make timely decisions in a fast-paced operation.
* Effective oral, written and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate expectations, performance, risks and recommendations to employees, leaders and senior management.
* Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook; familiarity with manufacturing, maintenance, warehouse and performance-reporting systems.

**EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE:** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Operations Management or a related field preferred; equivalent manufacturing leadership experience will be considered.
* Minimum 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including prior overall responsibility as a plant, site or operations leader for a large, complex manufacturing facility.
* Prior responsibility for multiple functions, including Production, Quality, Maintenance and Warehouse/Distribution operations, with demonstrated success improving plant performance.
* Beverage manufacturing experience strongly preferred; significant food manufacturing experience will also be considered.
* Experience leading a unionized manufacturing workforce strongly preferred.
* Experience managing operating budgets, labor costs, productivity, equipment reliability, quality, safety and overall plant performance required.
* Any equivalent combination of education, experience and training that provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS / WORK ENVIRONMENT / TRAVEL:** 

* Manufacturing, warehouse and office environments; regular presence on the production floor is required.
* Must be able to work around moving equipment, elevated noise levels, temperature variation and other conditions typical of a beverage manufacturing facility, with required personal protective equipment.
* Ability to move throughout the facility and occasionally lift, push or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to work a flexible schedule and respond to operational needs outside normal business hours; limited travel may be required.

**COMPENSATION RANGE:** 
Potential earning is from $190,000.00 - $215,000.00 annually
 
 
The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees and are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required by personnel so classified. Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of the company.
 
 

* We do not provide application status due to overwhelming volume. If your skills meet our needs, we will contact you to move forward in the process.\*

\*\*EOE without regard to race, color, religion, creed, affectional or sexual orientation or sex, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetics, veteran status, gender, gender identity, citizenship status, marital status, VEVRAA Federal Contractor.\*\*
 
\*\*\*If you have a disability and you need an accommodation to apply, please contact us at hiring@hongrp.com

records.title: Director, HR – U.S. Commercial & Manufacturing
records.description:
Vantive is a vital organ therapy company on a mission to extend lives and expand possibilities for patients and care teams everywhere. For 70 years, our team has driven meaningful innovations in kidney care. As we build on our legacy, we are deepening our commitment to elevating the dialysis experience through digital solutions and advanced services, while looking beyond kidney care and investing in transforming vital organ therapies. Greater flexibility and efficiency in therapy administration for care teams, and longer, fuller lives for patients— that is what Vantive aspires to deliver.

We believe Vantive will not only build our leadership in the kidney care space, it will also offer meaningful work to those who join us. At Vantive, you will become part of a community of people who are focused, courageous and don’t settle for the mediocre. Each of us is driven to help improve patients’ lives worldwide. Join us in advancing our mission to extend lives and expand possibilities.

This position serves as the senior strategic people leader and trusted advisor to the SVP – U.S. General Manager and the U.S. Executive Leadership Team, overseeing HR for U.S. Field Sales, U.S. Marketing, and U.S. Manufacturing (approximately 950 employees). The leader shapes and executes the HR strategy that enables business objectives and builds the organizational capability and culture required for sustained growth.

**Critical Responsibilities**

* Lead, develop, and inspire the HR team supporting these organizations, setting priorities, performance expectations, and a high-performing culture
* Sit on the U.S. Commercial Leadership Team and the Americas HR Leadership Team, building influential cross-functional partnerships
* Design and deliver business-specific HR solutions that measurably advance business outcomes
* Provide executive-level counsel to senior leaders, managers, and employees
* Provide thought leadership and accountability for culture, integration, organizational design, leadership development, and large-scale change management
* Apply strong analytical skills, strategic judgment, and financial acumen, including knowledge of the organization’s financial position, long-range plans, culture, and competitive landscape, to shape decisions and influence senior stakeholders
* Assess the effectiveness of the organization’s business model and dynamics, and lead realignment as needed to drive performance
* Lead strategic workforce planning and advise senior leadership on hiring, headcount, and organizational design decisions
* Advise site leaders and the HR team on manufacturing employee relations, engagement, and compliance, driving consistent HR practices across U.S. sites

**Risk, Governance & Compliance**

* Bring demonstrable experience in employee relations, labor relations, and compliance, and develop and manage the labor relations strategy
* Advise on organizational change related to automation, restructuring, new product launches, digital transformation, and expansion
* Partner with Legal to mitigate people-related risks and ensure alignment with local regulations and corporate standards

**Key Qualifications**

* Exceptional experience partnering with senior leaders, people managers, and employees in a highly matrixed, multi-site global environment
* Deep expertise across HR disciplines, including integration and transformation, talent acquisition, performance management, compensation, culture and engagement, change management, organizational design, and inclusion & diversity
* Demonstrated executive presence, with the ability to counsel and influence at the most senior levels, collaborate across the business and HR COEs, and communicate exceptionally well
* Proven ability to lead and develop HR professionals, including HR Business Partners, and build a high-performing HR organization
* Experience supporting manufacturing or operations environments, including partnering with plant leadership, managing hourly and salaried workforces, and analyzing labor cost, overtime, absenteeism, and staffing utilization metrics
* Ability to analyze data quickly and provide actionable, strategic business recommendations
* Proven track record of designing and implementing HR strategies that translate organizational strategy into the people agenda and drive measurable business results
* Advanced financial acumen, including the ability to connect people strategy to business financials
* Minimum Bachelor’s degree. MBA or Master’s degree in an HR discipline preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive HR experience, including 7+ years in HR Business Partner or senior HR leadership roles, leading teams and advising executive-level leaders. Health care, pharma, and commercial backgrounds preferred.

We understand compensation is an important factor as you consider the next step in your career. At Vantive, we are committed to equitable pay for all employees, and we strive to be more transparent with our pay practices. The estimated base salary for this position is $180,000 - $250,000 annually. The estimated range is meant to reflect an anticipated salary range for the position. We may pay more or less than the anticipated range based upon market data and other factors, all of which are subject to change. Individual pay is based on upon location, skills and expertise, experience, and other relevant factors. For questions about this, our pay philosophy, and available benefits, please speak to the recruiter if you decide to apply and are selected for an interview.

**US Benefits at Vantive**

This is where your well-being matters. Vantive offers comprehensive compensation and benefits packages for eligible roles. Our health and well-being benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage that start on day one, as well as insurance coverage for basic life, accident, short-term and long-term disability, and business travel accident insurance. Financial and retirement benefits include the Aon Pooled Employer Plan (“Aon PEP”), Vantive’s 401(k) retirement savings plan, to help you prepare for your future. The Aon PEP is designed to help improve retirement outcomes by providing retirement resources more efficiently. The plan offers a robust set of investment options, financial education, and a suite of resources to support your retirement goals.

We also offer Flexible Spending Accounts, educational assistance programs, and time-off benefits such as paid holidays, paid time off ranging from 20 to 35 days based on length of service, family and medical leaves of absence, and paid parental leave. Additional benefits include commuting benefits, the Employee Discount Program, the Employee Assistance Program (EAP), and childcare benefits. Join us and enjoy the competitive compensation and benefits we offer to our employees. For additional information regarding Vantive’s US Benefits, please speak with your recruiter or visit our Benefits site: Benefits | Vantive

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Vantive is an equal opportunity employer. Vantive evaluates qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, protected veteran status, disability/handicap status or any other legally protected characteristic. 
 
Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal

**Reasonable Accommodation**

Vantive is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities globally. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the application or interview process, please click on the link here and let us know the nature of your request along with your contact information. Form Link

**Recruitment Fraud Notice** 
 
Vantive has discovered incidents of employment scams, where fraudulent parties pose as Vantive employees, recruiters, or other agents, and engage with online job seekers in an attempt to steal personal and/or financial information. To learn how you can protect yourself, review our Recruitment Fraud Notice.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
At IEM, we're not just building innovative electrical distribution systems, we're shaping the future. IEM is dedicated to delivering world-class solutions for complex power needs. After 75 years, we continue to push the boundaries of what's possible. Whether you're an experienced professional or just starting out, you'll have the opportunity to contribute, grow, and make a lasting impact on industries that power the world's most dynamic markets.

IEM is seeking a Director of Operations to lead Medium Voltage Switchgear, Integrated Products, and Small Panels manufacturing in Jacksonville, Florida. This role owns safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, capacity, and team development across the assigned product lines.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on operations leader with experience scaling complex, high-mix manufacturing environments, building strong leaders, implementing Lean operating systems, and ensuring disciplined daily execution.

**Please note: This position requires 100% in-office presence in our** **Jacksonville****offices and does not offer remote work.**

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* Set and execute the operating strategy for Medium Voltage Switchgear, Integrated Products, and Small Panels.
* Align production, capacity, labor, scheduling, materials flow, maintenance, and support priorities with business objectives and customer commitments.
* Translate backlog and forecasted demand into practical labor, equipment, facility, material, and production capacity plans.
* Lead critical customer deliverables, production recovery plans, new-product introductions, and major internal initiatives.
* Provide timely operational updates, risk assessments, and recovery plans to the Vice President of Operations and Executive Leadership Team.
* Champion a culture where safety is a core operating value and leadership responsibility.
* Improve safety performance through hazard reduction, employee engagement, and proactive risk mitigation.
* Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, internal, and customer requirements, including OSHA, ISO, UL, and product-specific quality standards.
* Drive root-cause analysis and corrective action for nonconformances, defects, and recurring operational issues.
* Maintain readiness for customer audits, regulatory reviews, certifications, and changing compliance requirements.
* Build a continuous-improvement culture grounded in operational discipline, accountability, and fact-based problem-solving.
* Champion Lean practices such as daily management, visual management, standard work, takt alignment, flow, pull systems, workplace organization, and structured problem-solving.
* Establish and monitor KPIs for safety, quality, delivery, cost, labor productivity, yield, schedule attainment, throughput, work-in-process, and asset utilization.
* Use real-time operating data and visual management to identify risks, prioritize resources, and accelerate decisions.
* Reduce manufacturing costs through effective use of labor, equipment, facilities, materials, and capital.
* Partner with Finance on operating plans, budgets, variances, and cost-improvement commitments.
* Lead and develop Value Stream Managers, Operations Managers, and senior manufacturing leaders across the assigned product lines.
* Build a high-performing organization through selection, onboarding, coaching, performance management, succession planning, and leadership development.
* Strengthen frontline leadership through clear expectations, management routines, decision rights, and accountability.
* Foster teamwork, engagement, and ownership through visible leadership and consistent involvement.
* Lead organizational and cultural changes needed to support IEM's growth and increasing operational maturity.
* Partner with EHS, Planning, Engineering, Quality, Process Improvement, Supply Chain, Procurement, Human Resources, Finance, and other support teams.
* Coordinate cross-functional priorities to remove production barriers, improve manufacturability, resolve quality issues, and maintain production flow.
* Work with Engineering and Quality on new-product introductions, design changes, process qualification, corrective actions, and manufacturing readiness.
* Align production requirements with material availability, supplier performance, inventory objectives, and customer demand.

**Qualifications**
------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, Business, or a related field required; master's degree, MBA, or equivalent advanced education preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing or operations experience, including 5+ years in senior leadership roles.
* Experience leading large-scale, high-mix, multi-stage, engineered-to-order, configure-to-order, or vertically integrated manufacturing operations.
* Background in medium-voltage switchgear, electrical distribution equipment, integrated power systems, industrial controls, panel manufacturing, or a comparable technical manufacturing environment strongly preferred.
* Proven success improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, throughput, cost, and employee engagement.
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management systems, visual management, standard work, capacity planning, production flow, and plant layout optimization.
* Experience scaling operations, leading plant-wide initiatives, implementing automation, and introducing digital performance-management tools.
* Strong financial acumen, including budgeting, cost management, capital planning, and operational performance analysis.
* Ability to lead through complexity, set priorities, manage change, communicate effectively, and hold teams accountable for measurable results.
* Demonstrated career progression and potential to assume broader leadership responsibilities in a fast-paced, growth-oriented organization.

Compensation actually offered for this role will take into account internal equity and also may vary depending on the candidate's geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience among other factors.

**Why Join IEM**

At IEM, you'll join a team that powers some of the world's most ambitious projects. We're engineers, makers, and problem-solvers who thrive on tackling complex challenges and delivering solutions that keep industries moving forward. If you're driven, collaborative, and ready to make an impact, we'd love to hear from you. Your creativity and passion can help us achieve great things—come be part of the journey.

Learn more about IEM at https://www.iemfg.com

We offer comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support our employees' well-being, growth, and long-term success. View a snapshot of our benefits at https://www.iemfg.com/careers

**Recruiting Scams**

Beware of recruiting scams. IEM never charges candidates fees, and all recruiter emails come from an @iemfg.com address. If you suspect fraudulent activity, do not share personal information and report it to us at iemfg.com/contact

**Non-Discrimination Statement**

IEM does not discriminate against any applicant based on any characteristic protected by law.

records.title: Director, Manufacturing
records.description:
**Hyve Company Overview**
-------------------------

Hyve Solutions transforms complex engineering challenges into production reality for technology innovators building AI, cloud, and connected infrastructure. As a US-based manufacturing partner, the company rapidly delivers fast, agile execution through dep technical partnerships and co-innovation, and supply chain clarity. Hyve’s integrated ODM, CM, and SI capabilities eliminate vendor complexity while accelerating time-to-market with single-partner accountability from design through scale. The company co-innovates with deep engineering expertise, treating customer success as its own while building tomorrow's digital infrastructure.

 
 

**Director, Manufacturing**

**Location: Las Vegas, Nevada Reports directly to the Vice President of Manufacturing**

**Responsibilities**

* **Strategy: Develop and execute a manufacturing strategy aligned with Hyve's mission and values. Continuously refine and optimize processes for maximum efficiency at the primary location and across other manufacturing sites.**
* **Customer engagement: Serve as a direct interface with customer business, technical and operations teams.**
* **Planning and delivery: Build production plans, schedules and budgets that meet demand while maintaining world-class lean manufacturing and quality standards. Ensure on time, cost-effective delivery.**
* **Quality: Implement and maintain rigorous quality controls throughout the manufacturing process. Align to quality standards and monitor adherence to guarantee product excellence.**
* **Supply chain: Partner closely with customer and factory planning teams and 3PL teams to ensure reliable continuity of supply that supports production needs.**
* **Cost management: Control manufacturing costs by finding savings opportunities and managing headcount and budgets effectively.**
* **Compliance and safety: Stay current on industry regulations, safety standards and environmental requirements. Ensure full compliance with manufacturing operations.**
* **Continuous improvement: Drive initiatives that improve efficiency, quality and sustainability, apply lean principles and new technologies where they fit.**
* **Risk management: Identify and mitigate manufacturing risks to keep the operation resilient and adaptable.**
* **People leadership: Lead, develop and retain a multi-level manufacturing organization, building a strong bench of leaders.**

**Qualifications**

* **Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Manufacturing or a related field.**
* **15+ years of experience in manufacturing, sustaining, or product, process or design engineering. Experience with data infrastructure products, from peripherals through L10 or higher, is preferred.**
* **Strong knowledge of NPI and manufacturing processes, quality management, and rapid factory transitions and production ramps.**
* **10+ years of interaction with customers and internal executives at peer and senior levels.**
* **Proven record and formal training in team management, leadership and talent development.**
* **Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.**
* **Strong, data-driven problem-solving skills, including DOE, DFMEA and DFx.**
* **Familiarity with industry-standard manufacturing tools, shop floor control systems (MES) and operational metrics.**
* **A passion for environmental sustainability and commitment to Hyve's**

**What’s in it for you**
------------------------

Benefit Insurance

* Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
* Health Savings Account (HSA)
* Mental Health Care
* 401K with match
* Paid Holidays, Vacation & Sick Days
* Tuition Reimbursement
* Perks at Work
* LEAP Program
* MyFlexPay

***We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.***
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

records.title: Director of Production
records.description:
**Company Overview**

Delta Galil USA, Inc. is a global manufacturer and marketer of branded and private label apparel products for men, women and children. Since its inception in 1975, the company has continually endeavored to create products that follow a body-before-fabric philosophy, placing equal emphasis on comfort, aesthetics and quality. Delta Galil develops innovative seamless apparel, including bras, shapewear and socks; intimate apparel for women; underwear for men, including under its owned brands Schiesser, Eminence, Organic Basics and Athena; babywear, activewear, sleepwear and loungewear, including under its owned P.J. Salvage and Delta brands. Delta Galil also designs, develops, markets and sells branded denim and apparel under the brand 7 For All Mankind®, and ladies’ and kids’ apparel under the brand Splendid®. In addition, it sells its products under brand names licensed to the company, including adidas, Wolford, Wilson, Columbia, Tommy Hilfiger and others.

**Position Overview**

At Delta Galil, great product only matters if it reaches the shelf at the right cost, at the right quality and on time. As Director, Production & Sourcing, you’ll make that happen. You’ll own Sourcing and Production for your programs, from the first seasonal projection to the moment goods land at our Distribution Center, steering a global network of mills, factories and overseas offices that supply some of the biggest names in mass-market retail.

This is a role with real levers. You’ll negotiate the costs that shape the department’s margin, decide where programs are placed and how capacity is allocated, and lead the cross-functional team through every approval milestone, from BOM handoff to TOP. You’ll partner every day with Design, Planning and our Domestic and Offshore QA teams, and you’ll be the person everyone looks to when a delivery is at risk.

You’ll thrive here if you’re a natural negotiator and a hands-on leader who knows a garment down to its cost components, stays calm when a test fails or a vessel slips, and gets energy from turning a complex calendar into on-time deliveries.

**Key Responsibilities**

Sourcing, Costing & Vendor Strategy

* Share seasonal projections with mills and factories early, locking in key delivery dates and a generic TNA well ahead of order placement.
* Lead program-level cost negotiations that drive best costs and help the department meet or beat seasonal margin goals.
* Build and grow a strong vendor matrix that supports the business’s long-term needs.
* Place programs with overseas mills, factories and offices on time, with program-specific TNAs, the right capacity allocation and production plans that hit contracted deliveries.

Production Execution & Approvals

* Lead the cross-functional team through program TNAs, driving approvals from completed BOM handoff through color and components, fit, pre-production, testing and TOP.
* Work with stakeholders to resolve approval issues and testing failures quickly, escalating to leadership when needed.
* Assess production issues for delivery impact and lead cross-functional decisions on quality levels and ship-mode changes to protect customer deliveries.

Planning, Capacity & Delivery

* Partner with the Planning team to support the business at the right stock levels.
* Own and communicate monthly program capacity plans to mills and factories, flagging loading or capacity risks early.
* Keep POs current in the system, hold factories to timely bookings and approve vessel schedules that line up with customer deliveries.
* Build and maintain delivery reports for weekly team review.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

* Partner with Domestic and Offshore QA, sharing planned program allocation before placement.
* Champion critical QA steps before, during and at the end of production so product arrives at the Distribution Center free of quality issues and every customer order ships on time.
* Work with management to improve process flow and roll out new initiatives.

 
Requirements: 
 

* Minimum years of apparel experience across Product Development, Production, QA and Testing.
* Experience supplying a big-box, mass-market retailer such as Target or Walmart.
* Cut-and-sew knits experience (activewear strongly preferred).
* Deep knowledge of manufacturing, testing and quality control, including fabrics, trims and garment cost components (YY, CM, AU).
* A proven team leader with exceptional negotiation and problem-solving skills with factories and material suppliers.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to connect with factories, suppliers and internal teams at every level.
* Highly organized and detail-oriented, with strong follow-up, a sense of urgency and the ability to juggle multiple projects and teams.
* Advanced Excel skills (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables) and proficiency in Word and Outlook.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Activewear, intimates, loungewear, or knits experience.
* CPM and SMV knowledge, with a thorough understanding of cost component breakdowns.
* Experience traveling overseas to mills and factories.

**This is a hybrid role, with 4 days in our NJ office.**

**PAY RATE: $150,000/yr-$170,000/yr**

At Delta Galil, we strive to hire and nurture amazing talent. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience, specialized skills, and internal alignment.

DIVERSITY VISION STATEMENT:

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that welcomes and values the differences among all of our associates, customers, suppliers, and the communities in which we live and conduct business. We are an equal employment opportunity for minorities, females, protected veterans, and the disabled.

records.title: Plant Director
records.description:
**Accelerate the possible by joining a winning Amcor team that’s transforming the packaging industry and improving lives around the world.**
============================================================================================================================================

At Amcor, we unpack possibility through our innovative and responsible packaging to provide solutions that benefit our customers, our people and our planet. More than 10,000 consumers worldwide encounter our products every second and rely on us for safe access to food, medicine and other goods. We value their trust by making safety our guiding principle. It’s our core value and integral to how we do business.

Beyond this core principle, our shared values and behaviors unite us as we work together to elevate customers, shape lives and protect the future. We champion our customers and help them succeed. We play to win – adapting quickly in an everchanging world – and make smart choices to safeguard our business, our communities and the people we serve for generations to come. And we invest in our world-class team, empowering our colleagues to unpack their potential, because we believe when our people grow, so does our business.

To learn more about playing for Team Amcor, visit www.amcor.com I LinkedIn I Glassdoor I Facebook I YouTube

**Job Description**
===================

To manage and lead overall plant operations ensuring the achievement of plant targets for Safety, Quality, Service and Cost. This will be executed through providing strong leadership to the plant team and managing the systems, equipment, people and materials according to the established policies, procedures, specifications, and customer requirements. This individual reports directly to the Director-Manufacturing. The Plant Lead Team members will report directly to the Plant Manager (typically 6-10 direct reports) Scope for this Plant Manager role is a medium to large-sized facility with typically greater than 300 employees and mid to high-level complexity.

**WHAT YOU GET TO DO**

* Leads and drives plant safety culture and puts safety first in all responsibilities.
* Leads identification of opportunities and problem areas for targeted improvement by creating, reviewing and monitoring data or reports that show performance to KPI's. (specifically, safety, quality, waste, and productivity)
* Oversees all aspects of human capital planning & management for the facility, including HC goal setting, improvement targets for KPI's, salary planning, performance management.
* Attract, hire, develop direct reports and create strong succession plans
* Ensure compliance with department safety, product safety, fire protection, Company polices/procedures, and housekeeping programs.
* Ensures effective, timely and well-developed communications for all product associates.
* Manage process control initiatives by ensuring manufacturing SOP's exist, and that they are sufficient for quality, safety, and process control.
* Leads plant budgeting processes
* Ensures execution of plant Cap-Ex
* Lead and ensure growth of CI culture by providing resources, participating in teams, and leading teams as necessary.
* Ensures facility compliance with local, state and federal regulatory agencies.
* Drives employee engagement action planning for the facility
* Leads communication to all plant associates regarding business needs and results
* Leads efforts at Best Practice sharing with other facilities
* Meets safety targets and drives a safety culture and environment to send every employee home everyday without injury.
* Meets or exceeds plant business plan and KPI’s.
* Delivers on established budget.
* Best Practices leadership
* Effective, cost-efficient planning and utilization of manpower, materials and machinery.
* Strong Human Capital planning, development and management for the facility.
* Drives High Performance Culture
* Plant talent to deliver on plan

 **WHAT WE VALUE**
* Strong financial acumen
* Results Orientation / Delivers on Plan
* Team Leadership
* Develops Organizational Capability
* Strategic Orientation / Enterprise Thinker
* Collaboration & Influence
* Change Leadership
* Facility Business Acumen/Market Knowledge

**WHAT WE WANT FROM YOU**

* A Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business administration, or related field
* 10+ years of relevant experience in a production environment
* Demonstrated passion for safety
* 7+ years of leadership experience, preferably in flexible packaging
* Lives Amcor Values and leads by example
* Proven ability to lead and drive continuous improvement
* Strong Customer Service mindset
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Demonstrated knowledge of BNA customers and plant capabilities
* Demonstrated understanding of drivers of plant results, including ability to interpret financial results
* Demonstrated CI knowledge, Six Sigma Black Belt certification strongly preferred

**Our Expectations**
====================

We expect our people to be guided by The Amcor Way and demonstrate our Values every day to enable the business to win. We are winning when:

* Our people are engaged and developing as part of a high-performing Amcor team
* Our customers grow and prosper from Amcor’s quality, service, and innovation
* Our investors benefit from Amcor’s consistent growth and superior returns
* The environment is better off because of Amcor’s leadership and products

**Equal Opportunity** **Employer/Minorities/Females/Disabled/Veterans/Sexual** **Orientation/Gender Identity**
==============================================================================================================

Amcor is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you would like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please click on the *"Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal" Poster*. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please call 224-313-7000 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

**E-Verify**
============

We verify the identity and employment authorization of individuals hired for employment in the United States.

**Compensation**
================

The starting salary for this position is expected to be between $176,100 to $242,100 depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Base pay information is based on national averages and a geographic differential may be applied based on work location. Position may also be eligible for Amcor’s Management Incentive Plan / Sales Incentive Plan, which is an annual bonus program based on business and individual performance, as well as medical coverage and other health and welfare benefits. The salary range provided reflects the anticipated starting salary base pay for this role at the time of this posting and does not necessarily reflect full earning potential over the course of employment. This range is applicable to positions performed in jurisdictions with pay transparency requirements, including CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MD, MA, MN, NV, NJ, NY, RI, VT, WA, Washington DC, as well as remote roles that may be performed in these locations. Compensation for roles performed outside of these jurisdictions may vary. The Company reserves the right to modify this range at any time.

**Benefits**
============

When you join Amcor, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits and compensation package that includes:

* Medical, dental and vision plans
* Flexible time off, starting at 80 hours paid time per year for full-time salaried employees
* Company-paid holidays starting at 8 days per year and may vary by location
* Wellbeing program & Employee Assistance Program
* Health Savings Account/Flexible Spending Account
* Life insurance, AD&D, short-term & long-term disability, and voluntary benefits
* Paid Parental Leave
* Retirement Savings Plan with company match
* Tuition Reimbursement (dependent upon approval)
* Discretionary annual bonus program (initial eligibility dependent upon hire date)

records.title: Director of Signage Production
records.description:
The Production Director leads all signage manufacturing operations, including fabrication, wide-format printing, finishing, assembly, production quality and installation. This leader is accountable for meeting customer commitments, maximizing production capacity, controlling costs, and achieving departmental financial objectives. 
This is a high-accountability leadership role requiring operational expertise, financial discipline, and a growth mindset. The Director will build a high-performing team, establish clear expectations, improve productivity, eliminate bottlenecks, and ensure the department can scale efficiently as Strategic Factory grows. 
The objective is to deliver exceptional quality, flawless execution, and profitable growth through strong leadership, disciplined processes, and measurable results. 
Essential Responsibilities1. Financial Performance and Profitability

* Own departmental performance against revenue, gross margin, labor, material, and profitability targets.
* Monitor job costing, estimated versus actual labor, material usage, overtime, waste, and rework to protect margins.
* Establish cost controls and identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce expenses, and increase throughput.
* Align staffing, equipment, purchasing, and production capacity with work orders, forecasts, and company growth objectives.
* Partner with the VP of Signage, Finance, Sales, and Project Management to ensure production decisions support company-wide financial goals.

2. Production Leadership and Execution

* Lead all daily signage production operations, including fabricated signs, channel letters, dimensional signage, wide-format printing, finishing, and assembly.
* Own production scheduling, workflow, capacity planning, and on-time completion.
* Establish clear priorities, deadlines, and ownership across production teams.
* Coordinate with Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, and Installation to ensure projects move efficiently from order to completion.
* Identify constraints early, resolve production issues quickly, and maintain visibility into work in progress, material availability, and equipment utilization.
* Ensure production commitments are realistic, communicated, and consistently achieved.

3. Leadership and Accountability

* Build and develop a high-performing team focused on urgency, quality, teamwork, and results.
* Establish clear roles, measurable expectations, and accountability for supervisors and production employees.
* Hold team leaders accountable for schedules, staffing, productivity, quality, safety, and financial performance.
* Coach and develop supervisors to solve problems, make decisions, and own their results rather than relying on constant intervention.
* Address performance issues promptly, recognize strong performance, and ensure appropriate training and staffing.
* Foster a positive, high-energy culture that values continuous improvement, direct communication, and follow-through.
* Leadership standard: Set expectations, provide the tools to succeed, measure results, coach consistently, and hold people accountable.

4. Quality and Customer Satisfaction

* Establish quality standards for all fabricated, printed, and finished signage.
* Ensure work meets approved artwork, engineering specifications, material requirements, and customer expectations.
* Track defects, rework, scrap, and customer complaints; implement corrective actions to prevent recurring problems.
* Partner with Project Management and Installation to resolve issues and protect customer commitments.
* Promote a customer-first mindset in which quality, communication, and on-time delivery drive retention and future revenue.

5. Operational Excellence and Growth

* Continuously improve workflows, production methods, standard operating procedures, and equipment utilization.
* Eliminate bottlenecks, unnecessary handling, downtime, waste, and inefficient labor practices.
* Develop a scalable production plan aligned with sales forecasts and annual revenue goals.
* Identify staffing, equipment, facility, and technology investments needed to support growth, with clear financial justification.
* Make disciplined in-house versus outsourcing decisions based on cost, capacity, quality, and delivery.
* Use production data and performance scorecards to identify trends, assign corrective actions, and measure results.

6. Materials, Equipment, and Safety

* Manage material planning, inventory accuracy, purchasing coordination, and supplier performance.
* Control material waste and ensure supplies are available to meet production schedules without unnecessary inventory.
* Oversee preventive maintenance and ensure equipment is operated and maintained properly.
* Maintain a safe, organized production environment and enforce company safety policies and applicable OSHA requirements.
* Ensure required training, maintenance records, and safety procedures are consistently maintained.

7. Communication and Cross-Functional Leadership

* Provide regular reporting on financial performance, production schedules, capacity, staffing, quality, and operational risks.
* Communicate schedule changes, material shortages, and customer delivery risks proactively.
* Work collaboratively with Sales, Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, and Installation to achieve company objectives.
* Support leadership decisions, communicate priorities consistently, and focus on solutions rather than excuses.

The Director will be evaluated against established company targets, including:

* Financial: Revenue achievement, gross margin, labor costs, and departmental profitability.
* Execution: On-time delivery, schedule adherence, throughput, and production cycle time.
* Quality: Rework, scrap, defects, and customer complaints.
* Productivity: Labor efficiency, overtime, equipment utilization, and capacity.
* Growth: Ability to increase production volume while controlling costs and maintaining quality.
* Leadership: Staffing, employee development, accountability, and performance improvement.
* Operational discipline: Material waste, inventory accuracy, safety, and completion of improvement initiatives.
 
* **Requirements**

 

* 7-10 years of progressive experience in sign manufacturing, fabrication, wide-format printing, or a related production environment.
* At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams and preferably multiple production functions.
* Demonstrated experience with fabricated and printed signage, production scheduling, workflow management, and quality control.
* Proven ability to manage job costs, labor, materials, capacity, and profitability.
* Track record of improving productivity, quality, on-time delivery, and financial results.
* Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
* Experience with ERP/MIS systems, production reporting, and performance metrics.
* Knowledge of equipment maintenance, workplace safety, and manufacturing best practices.
* Relevant degree preferred; equivalent experience and demonstrated results will be considered.

Full Time

 

**Opportunity ID**

25267

**Job Description**

Greer Stop Nut, a Nashville, TN area fasteners manufacturing company, has an immediate opening for an experienced **Plant Manager**.

The Plant Manager is accountable for the safety, performance, and continuous improvement of our highly capable manufacturing operation. This role drives profitability and customer satisfaction through disciplined execution, people development, and the thoughtful application of automation, data, and AI-enabled tools to improve decision-making and operational efficiency.

As the site leader for Greer Stop Nut, the Plant Manager fosters a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement, ensuring alignment with broader business objectives while operating effectively within a centralized financial structure.

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Culture & Safety**

* Serve as the visible champion of safety, compliance, and ethical conduct, embedding EHS expectations into daily operations.
* Build a high-engagement culture focused on continuous improvement, learning, and problem solving.
* Develop, coach, and retain a versatile leadership team capable of operating in a lean, small-plant environment.

**Business Performance & Financial Stewardship**

* Drive plant-level financial performance, including cost control, productivity, working capital, and cash generation, within a roll-up financial model.
* Input to budgets, forecasts, and long-range plans; ensure disciplined execution against commitments.
* Ensure annual revenue, margin, and profitability targets for the facility are achieved.

**Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead day-to-day operations to consistently meet or exceed Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Productivity objectives.
* Drive lean manufacturing, TOC, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving disciplines.
* Lead root cause analysis and implement sustainable corrective actions; develop and execute recovery plans when performance gaps occur.
* Identify and execute high-impact improvement initiatives, balancing quick wins with long-term capability building.

**Customer, Product & Growth Focus**

* Own site-level customer performance metrics including quality, delivery, and responsiveness.
* Support new product introduction (NPI) and product/process development initiatives.
* Drive product line growth through operational readiness, capacity planning, and execution excellence.
* Communicate effectively with customers, suppliers, and internal stakeholders with professionalism and credibility.

**Innovation, Digital & AI Enablement**

* Leverage data, analytics, and emerging AI-enabled tools to improve:
* Champion automation, standardization, and smart use of technology appropriate to plant size and return on investment.
* Partner with Engineering, IT, and Operations Leadership to pilot and scale digital improvements aligned with company strategy.

**Cross-Functional Collaboration & Communication**

* Partner closely with EHS, Engineering, Quality, Sales, Finance, HR, and Supply Chain to ensure alignment and effective execution.
* Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with Division and Group leadership.
* Ensure clear, consistent communication across all levels of the organization.

**Required Skills & Capabilities**

* Strong leadership capability with heavy engagement with plant personnel in a hands-on environment.
* Demonstrated success driving results through lean manufacturing and continuous improvement.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a data-driven mindset.
* Ability to apply digital tools, analytics, and AI-enabled insights to manufacturing and business challenges.
* Proven ability to translate strategy into execution and deliver sustained results.
* Financial acumen with experience managing costs, productivity, and operating metrics.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills across technical and executive audiences.
* High adaptability and ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic environment.

**Preferred Skills**

* Working knowledge of Six Sigma, SPC, and advanced quality systems.
* Experience leading automation, digitalization, or smart factory initiatives.
* Project and program management experience with measurable outcomes.
* Industry experience in high volume metal machining manufacturing operations, or similar setting.

**Experience & Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent past experience. MS or MBA preferred.
* 7+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* Proven record of leading teams and delivering results through others.
* Demonstrated success in a machining or precision manufacturing environment.

*All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.*

Relocation is authorized for this position.

**National Security and Export Controls:** 
 
This position requires use of information or access to production processes subject to national security controls under U.S. export control laws and regulations (including, but not limited to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR)). To comply with those regulations, this position may require applicants to be U.S. Persons (i.e., U.S. citizens, U.S. lawful permanent residents, protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)), or eligible to obtain the required export authorizations from the U.S. Department of State or the U.S. Department of Commerce.

**About PCC**

**Greer Stop Nut**, located in Nashville, TN is a leading provider of specialty locking fasteners used in aerospace, military, and industrial applications and is proud to be part of the Precision Castparts Corp. (PCC) global family of manufacturing facilities.

With more than 120 operations and approximately 20,000 employees worldwide, Precision Castparts Corp. is the market leader in manufacturing large, complex structural investment castings, airfoil castings, forged components, aerostructures and highly engineered, critical fasteners for aerospace applications. In addition, we are the leading producer of airfoil castings for the industrial gas turbine market. We also manufacture extruded seamless pipe, fittings, and forgings for power generation and oil & gas applications; commercial and military airframe aerostructures; and metal alloys and other materials for the casting and forging industries. With such critical applications, we insist on quality and dependability – not just in the materials and products we make, but in the people we recruit.

PCC is relentless in its dedication to being a high-quality, low-cost and on-time producer; delivering the highest value to its customers while continually pursuing strategic, profitable growth.

In 2016, Berkshire Hathaway, led by Chairman and CEO Warren E. Buffett, acquired Precision Castparts Corp.

*Precision Castparts Corp. and its affiliates do not accept unsolicited resumes from search firms or employment agencies. Unsolicited resumes will become the property of Precision Castparts Corp & its affiliates, and no fee will be paid.*

records.title: Physical Plant Director - Deer Ridge
records.description:
We are seeking an knowledgeable and enthusiastic Maintenance Director to join our Physical Plant Department at Deer Ridge memory care!

**Full-time opportunity!**

**Earn between $30 and $2/hour, dependent on experience!**

**Multiple Shifts! MON - FRI.**

**Leadership opportunity!**

**BENEFITS**

* Health, Dental, Vision, Life, Accident, and other insurances
* Employer HSA Contributions
* Earn $500 through our referral program
* Paid Vacation, Sick Leave, and Holidays
* Work/Life Balance, consistent/flexible schedules
* Opportunity for growth within the organization
* Achievement Awards
* Complimentary meal during scheduled shift

**Who you are:**

You enjoy maintenance and effectively troubleshooting day-to-day issues. This role tracks and completes physical plant services to maintain the building and grounds of the community.

**What you'll do:**

* **This position is a hands-on Physical Plant Director position who will routinely complete small and large maintenance tasks on the community premises**
* Direct, coordinate, and complete physical plant services to maintain the building and grounds of the community
* Routinely inspect the physical plant and provide routine preventative maintenance within acceptable standards of practice
* Routinely coordinate, direct, and document required fire drills and fire drill training
* Establish and maintain a schedule of service of equipment and systems
* Maintain outside yard care, whether performed by facility staff or contract service
* Maintain facility to meet all regulatory requirements
* Painting inside and outside
* Maintain community building to meet all regulatory requirements
* Supervises Housekeeping Staff and Maintenance Assistant (if applicable)
* Perform other duties as assigned

**Qualifications:**

* Possess the diagnostic and mechanical skills and abilities necessary for accomplishing repairs on systems and buildings
* Supervisory skills and experience
* Must be drug-free and submit to drug screening upon hire and routinely
* Must be able to pass a criminal background check upon hire and as required by state regulations
* Ability to communicate effectively with residents, families, staff, vendors, and the general public

**ABOUT KOELSCH COMMUNITIES**

We are third-generation, family-owned, and operated. Koelsch Communities operates nearly 40 communities in eight states, with multiple new communities in development. Koelsch has led the Senior Living industry for over 65 years, delivering world-class customer service, home craftsmanship, and unprecedented amenities. Koelsch Communities strives to provide a positive, rewarding, and enjoyable environment to all of its employees and residents. After all, the common purpose at Koelsch Communities is: To create happiness by providing the finest living experiences anywhere.

Koelsch Communities is an equal opportunity employer and these protections extend to all management practices and decisions, including recruitment and hiring, appraisal systems, promotions/demotions, training, and any other career development programs. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status (physical or mental), family medical history, genetic information, political affiliation or any other non-merit-based factors.

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
**Plant Manager**

**Nedcon USA LLC | Shelbyville, KY**

**About the Opportunity**

Nedcon USA LLC is seeking an experienced Plant Manager to lead our growing manufacturing facility in Shelbyville, Kentucky. Opened in 2024, designed using the proven manufacturing model and technology successfully utilized by Nedcon's established operations in the Czech Republic the facility utilizes state-of-the-art roll forming and welding technology to manufacture steel racking system components for the North American market.

This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for the overall performance of the facility, including safety, quality, delivery, productivity, cost management, and employee development. The Plant Manager will lead a developing operation and play a key role in future growth, process optimization, automation, and capacity expansion.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations, including roll forming, welding, maintenance, production planning, and material flow.
* Drive performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity.
* Develop and mentor supervisors and production leaders while building a strong, engaged workforce.
* Champion a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
* Monitor and improve key performance indicators, including OEE, labor efficiency, scrap reduction, and on-time delivery.
* Lead Lean Manufacturing and process improvement initiatives.
* Manage plant budgets, capital projects, and resource planning.
* Collaborate with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and European technical teams to support operational and strategic objectives.
* Support facility growth, automation initiatives, and future production expansion.

**Qualifications**

**Required:**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business, or a related field.
* 7+ years of manufacturing leadership experience with responsibility for production or plant operations.
* Proven success leading teams and improving operational performance.
* Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, safety systems, quality systems, and continuous improvement methodologies.

**Preferred:**

* Experience in roll forming, steel processing, metal fabrication, welding, or related industrial manufacturing.
* Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or Operational Excellence experience.
* Experience working within an international manufacturing organization.
* SAP or ERP system experience.

**Why Join NEDCON?**

This is an opportunity to shape the future of a growing manufacturing operation and make a significant impact on the development of Nedcon's North American production footprint. You will work with advanced manufacturing technologies, a collaborative leadership team, and a global organization committed to innovation and operational excellence.

**About NEDCON**

Since 1969, NEDCON has been a leader in storage systems, offering solutions from manual warehouse racks to complex automated systems. We design, test, and manufacture our products in-house to ensure the highest quality and reliability. Our storage solutions serve international organizations, including prominent e-commerce companies and supermarkets. With headquarters in the Netherlands and offices in Europe and the United States, our employees work together to create a family-like culture. Our belief is that our employees and culture are just as important to the company as serving our customers. We place a high value on building a team and working environment where individuals can succeed professionally and personally.

We'd love to have you join our NEDCON family. As a team member at NEDCON, you can expect to make a difference through your work, to have a direct impact on the achievement of our company growth and mission to serve our customers and to have room for fun and fulfillment in your daily life.

View our US production facility: https://youtu.be/uOuxJzsOBcw?si=wKm7-CgqJbhgOc4W

Nedcon USA is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace and consider all qualified applicants for employment.

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Parental leave
* Professional development assistance
* Referral program
* Retirement plan
* Tuition reimbursement
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* Do you have experience in the Roll forming industry, if not then what manufacturing or steel process experience do you have?
* Have you been accountable for plant KPIs such as OEE, scrap, labor productivity, and on-time delivery?
* What continuous improvement methodologies have you led?
* How many direct and indirect employees have you managed?

Experience:

* Manufacturing Leadership: 5 years (Required)

Work Location: In person
