records.title: Director of Facility Operations
records.description:
**Location**: Detroit, MI 48202 
**Job Type**: Full-Time 
**Schedule:** Primarily weekdays, with flexibility for evenings, weekends, holidays, and emergency response as needed 
**Salary:** $65,000–$75,000 annually 
**Work Location:** On-site

**About Michigan Science Center** 
The Michigan Science Center (Mi-Sci) is a nonprofit organization dedicated to inspiring curiosity and a lifelong passion for science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM). Through interactive exhibits, educational programs, and hands-on experiences, Mi-Sci connects people of all ages with science in an engaging and welcoming environment.

**Position Overview** 
The Michigan Science Center is seeking an experienced, hands-on Director of Facility Operations to oversee the daily operations, maintenance, safety, and overall readiness of its facility. 
Reporting to the Managing Director of Experience, the Director of Facility Operations will be responsible for managing building systems, preventive maintenance, contractors, safety procedures, and facility improvement projects. This position requires a proactive leader who can balance long-term planning with day-to-day operational needs. 
The ideal candidate has strong technical knowledge of commercial building systems, experience managing vendors and maintenance operations, and the ability to respond effectively to facility-related issues in a busy, public-facing environment.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily facility operations, ensuring the building remains safe, functional, and ready for staff and visitors.
* Manage and monitor building systems, including HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, building automation, elevators, and other essential infrastructure.
* Develop and maintain preventive maintenance schedules, inspections, work orders, and equipment service records.
* Coordinate and supervise maintenance, custodial, and specialized contractors, ensuring timely and quality service.
* Manage facility operating budgets, service contracts, repair priorities, and capital improvement planning.
* Oversee building safety, security, emergency preparedness, fire and life safety systems, and regulatory compliance.
* Respond to facility emergencies, equipment failures, and operational concerns, coordinating repairs and communicating updates to relevant teams.
* Supervise facility personnel and contractors, providing clear direction, accountability, and support.
* Collaborate with internal departments to coordinate building access, events, maintenance activities, and operational needs.
* Support building opening and closing procedures, including occasional evenings, weekends, holidays, and Manager on Duty (MOD) assignments.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum of 5 years of progressively responsible experience in commercial, institutional, museum, campus, or similar complex facility operations.
* At least 2 years of supervisory, contractor management, or facilities leadership experience.
* Working knowledge of commercial HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and building maintenance systems.
* Experience coordinating preventive maintenance, repairs, contractors, and service schedules.
* Ability to assess operational issues, prioritize repairs, and coordinate appropriate technical support.
* Strong communication, organizational, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work on-site and respond to occasional after-hours facility needs.
* Associate degree, technical diploma, apprenticeship, relevant professional training, or equivalent substantial experience in facilities management or a related field.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, or a related field.
* Experience managing building automation systems, fire and life safety systems, and facility operating budgets.
* Previous experience working in museums, educational institutions, or other public-facing facilities.
* Relevant certifications such as Certified Facility Manager (CFM), Facility Management Professional (FMP), OSHA safety training, or EPA Section 608 certification.

**What We Offer** 
**Salary:** $65,000–$75,000 annually, based on qualifications and experience. 
**Benefits Include:** 
401(k) 
Health, dental, and vision insurance 
Life insurance 
Paid time off (PTO) 
Employee assistance program (EAP) 
Flexible spending account (FSA) 
Health savings account (HSA)

**Equal Employment Opportunity** 
Michigan Science Center is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, national origin, citizenship status, disability, race, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, public assistance status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

Michigan Science Center encourages candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply. Applicants who may not meet every listed qualification but believe their skills and experience make them well-qualified are also encouraged to apply.

Pay: $65,000.00 - $75,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Vision insurance

Application Question(s):

* How many years of experience do you have in commercial, institutional, or complex building facility operations?
* How many years of experience do you have supervising facility staff, managing contractors, or leading maintenance operations?
* Do you have hands-on experience overseeing commercial HVAC, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, or building automation systems?
* Are you able to work on-site in Detroit, MI, and accommodate occasional evenings, weekends, holidays, and emergency calls as needed?

Education:

* Associate (Preferred)

Ability to Commute:

* Detroit, MI 48202 (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

records.title: Director, Contract Operations
records.description:
We are on the front line of recruitment, enabling organizations to hire smarter and onboard faster. At First Advantage (Nasdaq: FA), people are at the heart of everything we do. From our customers and partners to our greatest advantage — our team members.

Say hello to a rewarding career and come join a leading provider of mission-critical background screening solutions to some of the most recognized Fortune 100 and Global 500 brands.

**About First Advantage**

First Advantage (NASDAQ: FA) is a leading provider of global software and data in the HR technology industry. Enabled by proprietary technology and AI, First Advantage’s platforms, data, and APIs power comprehensive employment background screening, identity solutions, and verification services.

Headquartered in Atlanta, GA, we have an internationally distributed workforce of about 10,000 employees spanning 17 countries. With a strong emphasis on innovation, automation, and customer success, First Advantage empowers 80,000 organizations to modernize their hiring and onboarding processes on a global scale.

**What You'll Do**

**Director, Global Contract Operations** is responsible for establishing the operational strategy, governance framework, technology roadmap, and performance standards for the Company's global contracting function.

This role serves as the senior operational leader within Legal responsible for contract intake governance, workflow administration, process transformation, contract lifecycle management (CLM) optimization, contracting technology enablement and operational support services.

The position partners closely with Legal leadership, Sales, Procurement, Compliance, IT, Finance, and regional business leaders to develop scalable contracting capabilities that support business growth, operational efficiency, risk mitigation, and governance objectives.

The Director serves as the primary operational liaison between Legal leadership and business stakeholders, translating approved legal policies, playbooks, and contracting standards into sustainable processes, systems, controls, and service delivery models.

While this role does not make legal risk determinations or provide legal advice, it is accountable for enterprise-wide contracting operational effectiveness, contracting technology strategy, workflow governance, and continuous improvement initiatives supporting the Legal function.

**This role is 100% work from home role within the United States.**

**Strategic Leadership & Operating Model Ownership**

* Define and execute the global contract operations strategy, roadmap, and operating model.
* Establish enterprise-wide standards for contract intake, prioritization, assignment, workflow execution, escalation and service delivery.
* Lead alignment of contracting operations across regions, business units, functions and contract types.
* Identify operational risks, scalability challenges, and process inefficiencies and develop long-term solutions.
* Serve as executive owner of contracting operational processes, procedures, governance standards, and service delivery models
* Advise senior leadership on operational strategy, resource planning, and transformation opportunities.

**Process Transformation & Continuous Improvement**

* Lead enterprise-wide process improvement initiatives focused on efficiency, standardization, automation, and scalability.
* Own and continuously improve the global intake, triage, assignment, and workflow management framework.
* Establish and maintain global SOPs, process maps, RACI models, and operational documentation standards.
* Sponsor cross-functional initiatives that improve contracting effectiveness and stakeholder experience.
* Drive implementation of best practices, automation opportunities, and operational controls across the contract lifecycle.
* Lead remediation efforts for systemic operational bottlenecks and recurring process issues.

**People Leadership & Organizational Capability**

* Lead and develop contract intake and administrative support resources responsible for contracting workflow coordination, intake management, and operational support.
* Establish performance expectations, training plans, and workload management practices for operational support personnel
* Partner with Legal leadership to ensure appropriate resource alignment and operational support for contracting activities.
* Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and customer service.
* Provide oversight for operational support activities that facilitate efficient contract administration and workflow execution.

**Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) Strategy & Technology Enablement**

* Serve as business owner for contract operations technology, CLM adoption, workflow optimization and related operational systems.
* Partner with Legal, IT, Procurement, Sales, and business stakeholders to define CLM priorities, enhancements, integrations, and future-state capabilities.
* Lead operational readiness activities including UAT, change management, training, adoption, and post-implementation optimization.
* Provide oversight of CLM administration activities, including system configuration requests, metadata governance, user support, training, and enhancement prioritization.
* Drive technology-enabled transformation initiatives that improve visibility, efficiency, scalability, and compliance.
* Ensure CLM capabilities align with contracting strategy, operational objectives, and business requirements.

**Operational Performance, Metrics & Executive Visibility**

* Define the contract operations reporting strategy and performance management framework.
* Establish key performance indicators, service level expectations, and operational health metrics.
* Monitor service levels, turnaround times, workloads, backlog trends, resource utilization, and operational risks.
* Provide executive leadership with actionable insights, trend analysis, and strategic recommendations.
* Utilize operational data to drive investment decisions, resource planning, prioritization, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish executive visibility into contracting performance and operational effectiveness.

**Governance, Controls & Risk Alignment**

* Lead operational governance associated with approved contracting policies, procedures, workflows, and controls.
* Partner with Legal and Compliance leadership to ensure operational alignment with enterprise risk management objectives.
* Establish standards for documentation, approvals, escalations, and process compliance.
* Ensure operational readiness for audits, regulatory requirements, and governance reviews.
* Support enterprise initiatives requiring contract operations leadership, governance oversight, or implementation support.
* Maintain operational frameworks that support risk mitigation, consistency, accountability, and compliance.

**Qualifications**

* Experience leading global contract operations, legal operations, compliance operations, or business operations functions.
* Demonstrated success developing and executing operational strategy and transformation initiatives.
* Proven ability to build scalable operating models, governance frameworks, and performance management programs.
* Experience leading enterprise process improvement, workflow optimization, automation, and technology adoption initiatives.
* Strong executive presence and ability to influence senior leaders across multiple functions.
* Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, and change management skills.
* Strong analytical, organizational, and strategic planning capabilities.
* Experience leading geographically dispersed teams and cross-functional initiatives.

**Preferred:**

* Experience supporting legal, contracting, compliance, procurement, or commercial organizations.
* Experience with CLM platforms (IntelAgree, Icertis, Ironclad, Agiloft, DocuSign CLM, etc.).
* Experience with Salesforce, CPQ platforms, workflow automation tools, and enterprise technology implementations.
* Experience leading digital transformation and AI-enabled process initiatives.
* Project management and organizational change management experience.
* Experience supporting global operations across multiple regions and business units.

**What You Will Need to be Successful:**

**Education:**

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience; Juris Doctor preferred.

**Experience:**

* 10+ years of experience in one or more of the following:
 + Contract Operations
 + Legal Operations
 + Contract Management
 + Compliance Operations
 + Business Operations
 + Process Management
* 7+ years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for leading globally distributed teams.
* Demonstrated experience leading enterprise process transformation, technology implementation, governance programs, or operational excellence initiatives.

**Why Join Us at First Advantage?**

At First Advantage, team members are united around a noble purpose: helping organizations to safeguard their workplaces and manage risk. The company’s culture is shaped by its core values — Authenticity, Curiosity, Integrity, Teamwork, Customer-Inspired — empowering team members to bring their best ideas forward, collaborate across departments, and make a real impact.

First Advantage offers a variety of culture programs and benefits designed to enhance employee experience and development.

* Employee Impact Groups
* FA Cares volunteer opportunities
* Mentorship Advantage Program
* SOAR, award-winning manager development program

Additional benefits offered include:

* Ability to work remotely
* Medical, Vision, Dental, and supplementary benefit plans, including paid Parental Leave and Bereavement.
* 401k with an employer match and an Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP).
* Competitive and flexible Paid Time Off (PTO) and 8 paid company holidays.
Volunteer Time Off Policy (VTOP) up to 10 hours a year. 

 

**What Are You Waiting For? Apply Today!**

You have learned a little about us today – we want to learn about you! If you think this position and our company are a great fit for your areas of interest and expertise, tell us about you by applying now!

*The salary range for this position is approximately $145K-$175K base annually. This range reflects our good faith estimate to pay fairly as to what our ideal candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on the selected candidate’s experience, industry knowledge, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the interview process*

**We have great people here and are looking for more. Come join us!**

Follow us:

* Facebook
* Instagram
* LinkedIn
* X
* YouTube

***Equal Employment Opportunities at First Advantage*** 
*First Advantage is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to providing a workplace and recruitment process that is free from unlawful discrimination, harassment, and retaliation. Employment decisions at First Advantage are based solely on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We do not discriminate in any aspect of employment on the basis of race, color, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, religion, creed, sex, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital or family status, pregnancy, age, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.*

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
Description:

**Position Summary:**

The Director of Operations is responsible for the strategic leadership, oversight, and continuous improvement of the Bank's operational functions, systems, and processes. This position provides leadership to the Operations Manager, Treasury Management Sales Officer, and operational staff while ensuring operational excellence, regulatory compliance, risk mitigation, process efficiency, and exceptional employee and customer experiences.

The Director of Operations serves as the Bank's primary business owner for the core processing system and related operational technologies. This role is responsible for maintaining strong relationships with the Bank's core provider and other operational vendors, leading system implementations and enhancements, evaluating operational efficiencies, and ensuring operational resources effectively support the Bank's strategic objectives.

The Director of Operations partners closely with Senior Management, Compliance, Accounting, Retail Banking, Information Technology, and other committees to ensure operational processes, controls, and technologies remain efficient, scalable, and aligned with organizational goals. This position is expected to champion innovation, continuous improvement, and operational excellence throughout the organization.

**Duties and Responsibilities:**

* Directly supervises the Operations Manager and Treasury Management Sales Officer, providing leadership, coaching, performance management, and professional development while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and exceptional service.
* Provides strategic oversight of the Bank's operational functions and develops initiatives that improve efficiency, service quality, scalability, operational effectiveness, and overall customer and employee experience.
* Serves as the primary business owner and relationship manager for the Bank's core processing provider and related operational systems, leading system enhancements, upgrades, conversions, integrations, testing, implementation, training, and user communication.
* Manages relationships with operational vendors and third-party service providers, ensuring service effectiveness and value, regulatory compliance, and identification of technology solutions that improve operational performance.
* Leads operational projects, process improvement initiatives, and cross-functional efforts that streamline workflows, reduce risk, strengthen controls, and enhance service delivery throughout the organization.
* Develops and monitors operational performance metrics and reporting to evaluate departmental effectiveness, identify opportunities for improvement, and support strategic decision-making.
* Ensures operational activities comply with applicable laws, regulations, policies, and internal controls through effective risk management, policy administration, and support of internal and external audits and examinations.
* Serves as the Bank's operational subject matter expert and provides leadership in resolving escalated operational and customer service issues while ensuring responsive support to employees and customers.
* Partners with Senior Management and department leaders to ensure operational processes, controls, and technologies align with organizational objectives and strategic priorities.
* Maintains current knowledge of banking regulations, industry trends, operational technologies, and best practices.
* Performs other duties as assigned.

**Schedule**: Monday-Friday 8:00am-5:00pm

Requirements:

* Seven (7) years banking experience with significant operational responsibilities.
* Three (3) years leadership or management experience.
* Experience with core banking systems and operational technologies.
* Strong team development, project management, and organizational skills.
* Excellent analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, communication, and interpersonal skills.
* Ability to analyze operational workflows, implement process improvements, and effectively manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
* Ability to lead organizational change and influence cross-functional teams.

**Desired Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**

* Bachelor degree in Business Administration, Accounting, Finance, Management, or related field.
* Community banking experience strongly preferred.
* Extensive knowledge of bank operations, deposit services, payment systems, and operational processes.
* Strong understanding of banking regulations including ACH/NACHA, wire transfer requirements, BSA/AML, Reg E, Reg CC, CIP, and deposit compliance requirements.
* Experience administering or supporting core banking systems and operational software platforms.
* Experience leading projects, system implementations, process improvements, or core conversions.
* Strong technology aptitude and ability to evaluate and implement operational solutions.

**Questions on the role? Email us at HR@riverbank.biz.**

River Bank provides a diverse and inclusive work environment. We are an equal opportunity employer dedicated to hiring individuals with disabilities and protected veterans. EOE M/F/D/V

At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

records.title: Director of Operations
records.description:
**It’s not just a job. It’s a mission.**

Altruix is a high-touch pharmacy dedicated to serving behavioral health and intellectual and developmental disability populations. Through our pharmacy expertise, and specialized packaging, we promote medication adherence and improve patient outcomes. Our services help clients take medications as prescribed while reducing administrative burden for providers. Altruix customers achieve measurable results, including 90% adherence rates and a 40% reduction in ER and hospital-related costs. Learn more at www.altruix.com.

Altruix is seeking an experienced **Director of Operations** for the strategic and operational leadership of multiple pharmacy locations within an assigned region. This position provides oversight of pharmacy operations, regulatory compliance, financial performance, workforce management, customer satisfaction, and business growth initiatives.

The Director of Operations partners closely with Pharmacists-in-Charge (PICs), corporate leadership, clients, and regulatory agencies to ensure safe, compliant, efficient, and profitable pharmacy operations while supporting exceptional patient and customer service.

This role requires extensive field presence and direct operational oversight of assigned pharmacy locations. The Director of Operations is expected to spend approximately 80% of working time onsite at pharmacy locations, client facilities, or traveling between sites. Candidates should reside on the East Coast and be able to travel frequently as business needs require.

**Compensation:** $175,000 to $195,000 per year.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

***Operational Leadership***

* Provide leadership, direction, and oversight for operations across multiple pharmacy locations
* Develop, implement, and monitor operational strategies that drive efficiency, quality, productivity, and service excellence
* Ensure consistent execution of company policies, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and best practices across all assigned sites
* Identify operational opportunities and implement process improvement initiatives to enhance workflow efficiency and patient outcomes
* Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational metrics to ensure achievement of business objectives.

 

***Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management***

* Ensure pharmacy operations remain compliant with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations, including Board of Pharmacy requirements, DEA regulations, HIPAA requirements, and other applicable healthcare regulations
* Partner with pharmacy leadership to prepare for and manage regulatory inspections, audits, and accreditation activities
* Maintain accountability for controlled substance security, diversion prevention, inventory controls, and loss prevention programs
* Investigate operational compliance concerns and implement corrective action plans as necessary

 

***Financial Management***

* Maintain accountability for the financial performance of assigned pharmacy locations
* Monitor and manage labor expenses, staffing utilization, productivity, inventory management, purchasing activities, collections, and other financial metrics
* Develop and execute operational plans to achieve budgeted revenue, expense, profitability, and growth targets
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends and recommend strategic improvements

 

***Leadership & Talent Development***

* Develop, mentor, and retain high-performing pharmacy leaders, including Pharmacists in-Charge and site management teams
* Provide ongoing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development opportunities for employees
* Foster a culture of accountability, engagement, continuous improvement, and 
 operational excellence
* Conduct performance evaluations and support corrective action, employee relations, and succession planning activities as appropriate
* Ensure all employees complete required training and maintain necessary licensure and certifications

 

***Customer & Client Relations***

* Establish and maintain strong relationships with clients, prescribers, facility leadership, and key business partners
* Serve as a primary operational liaison between pharmacy locations and customers
* Promote a patient-centered culture focused on service excellence and responsiveness
* Address operational concerns and customer service issues in a timely and effective manner

 

***Business Growth & Site Development***

* Support organizational growth initiatives through implementation of new pharmacy locations, service lines, and client partnerships
* Lead operational planning associated with pharmacy startups, licensing activities, facility build-outs, staffing, training, and go-live readiness
* Identify opportunities to increase prescription volume, expand services, improve market penetration, and strengthen client relationships
* Collaborate with executive leadership on strategic planning and organizational growth initiatives

 

***Expectations***

* Achieve established operational, financial, compliance, quality, and customer service goals across all assigned pharmacy locations
* Maintain full compliance with applicable federal, state, Board of Pharmacy, DEA, HIPAA, and company requirements
* Ensure pharmacy locations operate efficiently, consistently, and in accordance with established policies, procedures, and quality standards
* Develop, mentor, and retain effective Pharmacy Managers, Pharmacists-in-Charge (PICs), and site leadership teams
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance operational efficiency, patient outcomes, customer satisfaction, and financial performance
* Partner effectively with clients, prescribers, facility leadership, and internal stakeholders to support operational excellence and business growth
* Maintain a visible leadership presence throughout the assigned region through regular onsite visits, operational reviews, employee coaching, and stakeholder engagement
* Travel extensively, including overnight travel as needed, and spending approximately 80% of working time onsite at pharmacy locations, customer sites, or in transit between locations to provide operational oversight and leadership support
* Demonstrate sound judgment, professionalism, and discretion when handling 
 confidential, sensitive, or business-critical information

 

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business administration, healthcare administration, pharmacy, or related field
* Minimum of five (5) years of progressive leadership experience in pharmacy operations, healthcare operations, or multi-site management
* Experience managing operational performance, compliance, staffing, and budgets across multiple locations
* Valid driver's license and ability to travel extensively
* PharmD degree, MBA, MHA, or other advanced business or healthcare-related degree
* Seven (7) or more years of pharmacy operations leadership experience. 
 Long-term care, institutional, specialty pharmacy, or closed-door pharmacy experience
* Experience launching new pharmacy locations and managing regulatory licensing activities

 

**BENEFITS:**

* Salary: $175,000 to $195,000 based on experience annually. Compensation will be commensurate with equity and experience for roles of similar scope and responsibility
* Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, and Long-Term Disability
* 401(k) program
* Paid time off
* Paid holidays

 

**EEOC:**

Altruix is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate in recruiting, hiring, placement, training, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfers, leaves of absence, compensation, or other employment practices based on any protected characteristic under federal, state, or local law. Altruix is a drug-free workplace and requires pre-employment drug and alcohol testing as a condition of employment.

records.title: Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations
records.description:
**Plant Manager - Manufacturing Operations**
--------------------------------------------

**Location:** Warren, MI 
**Work Model:** On-Site 
**Employment Type:** Full-Time 
**Reports To:**General Manager

**About SLPT**
--------------

**SLPT** is a manufacturing organization committed to delivering quality, reliability, and operational excellence for our customers. Located in Warren, Michigan, we take pride in building a culture where safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement drive everything we do.Our success starts with our people. We believe the best results come from empowered leaders who are willing to take ownership, develop talent, solve challenges, and continually raise the bar for performance. From the production floor to the leadership team, we foster an environment where employees are respected, supported, and encouraged to grow professionally.As we continue to invest in our operations, technology, and workforce, we are seeking leaders who are passionate about manufacturing excellence and motivated by the opportunity to make a measurable impact. The Plant Manager plays a critical role in shaping plant culture, driving continuous improvement, developing future leaders, and ensuring we consistently deliver exceptional results for our customers.

**Why Join SLPT?**
------------------

* Lead a high-impact manufacturing operation with significant responsibility and visibility.
* Influence plant strategy, operational performance, and business growth.
* Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives that create meaningful results.
* Partner with a collaborative leadership team focused on innovation and operational excellence.
* Develop and mentor employees while building a culture of accountability, engagement, and success.
* Join an organization that values strong leadership, problem-solving, and professional growth.

**At SLPT, you'll have the opportunity to make a lasting impact on our people, our customers, and the future of our manufacturing operations.**

**About the Role**
------------------

Are you a hands-on manufacturing leader who thrives in a fast-paced production environment? We are seeking an experienced **Plant Manager**to lead all aspects of our Warren, Michigan manufacturing operation. In this role, you will oversee safety, quality, production, delivery performance, cost management, and employee development across a 24-hour operation.You will play a key role in driving operational excellence, implementing Lean Manufacturing initiatives, and developing high-performing teams while ensuring customer expectations and business objectives are consistently achieved. The ideal candidate brings strong leadership experience, a passion for continuous improvement, and a proven track record of delivering results in a multi-shift manufacturing environment.

**What You Will Do**
--------------------

* Lead daily manufacturing operations across multiple shifts, ensuring achievement of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost goals.

records.title: Director, Quality (Mentor, OH or Plymouth, MN onsite based)

postedPay.title: Director, Quality (Mentor, OH or Plymouth, MN onsite based)

records.description:
**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.
  
  
Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.
  
  
**What You’ll Do As a Director Quality**

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:

+ Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
+ Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
+ Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
+ Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
+ Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
+ Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
+ Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
+ Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.

* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**Required**
**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.
* Strong expertise in analytical methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement methods.
* Excellent interpersonal, as well as verbal and written communication skills in order to develop and maintain rapport and effective internal and external relationships to support business success.
* The ability to work hard and deliver results under pressure, as well as the willingness to address and shift priorities in rapidly changing markets.

**Preferred**

* Advanced degree.
* Experience with statistical analysis software and Visio.
* Experience in medical device industry.

**Other**

* Excellent problem-solving skills.
* Focus on identification of potential issues and continuous improvement.
* Experience working on cross-functional teams and on own initiative.
* Demonstrated excellent organizational, oral, and written communications skills.
* Must have PC experience, as well as working familiarity of desktop applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

**What STERIS Offers**
We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and financial future.
  
  
**Here Is a Brief Overview Of What We Offer**

* Market competitive pay
* Extensive paid time off and (9) added holidays
* Excellent healthcare, dental, and vision benefits
* Long/short term disability coverage
* 401(K) with company match
* Maternity and parental leave
* Additional add on benefits/discounts for programs such as pet insurance
* Tuition reimbursement and continued educational programs
* Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career

Pay range for this opportunity is $144,500.00 - $187,000.00. This position is eligible for bonus participation.
  
  
Minimum pay rates offered will comply with county/city minimums, if higher than range listed. Pay rates are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to local labor market costs, years of relevant experience, education, professional certifications, foreign language fluency, etc.
  
  
STERIS offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits portfolio. Click here for a complete list of benefits: STERIS Benefits
  
  
Open until position is filled.
  
  
STERIS is a leading global provider of products and services that support patient care with an emphasis on infection prevention. WE HELP OUR CUSTOMERS CREATE A HEALTHIER AND SAFER WORLD by providing innovative healthcare and life sciences products and services around the globe. For more information, visit www.steris.com.
  
  
If you need assistance completing the application process, please call 1 (440) 392.7047. This contact information is for accommodation inquiries only and cannot be used to check application status.
  
  
STERIS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity to ensure that persons are recruited, hired, trained, transferred and promoted in all job groups regardless of race, color, religion, age, disability, national origin, citizenship status, military or veteran status, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth and related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, and any other category protected by federal, state or local law. We are not only committed to this policy by our status as a federal government contractor, but also we are strongly bound by the principle of equal employment opportunity.
  
  
The full affirmative action program, absent the data metrics required by
  
  

* 60-741.44(k), shall be available to all employees and applicants for employment for inspection upon request. The program may be obtained at your location’s HR Office during normal business hours.

records.title: Global Director of Quality
records.description:
General Summary
  
  
The Global Director of Quality is responsible for oversight of Quality Management and Continuous Improvement Programs for Team Industrial Services globally. The position is ultimately responsible for all corporate and Divisional Quality and Continuous support personnel. The successful candidate provides the necessary management and oversight to ensure the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of TEAM’s Quality Management System (QMS) as well as the supplemental Quality Control and Technical programs. Position is responsible for managing and coordinating all Quality support activities relating to the execution of the Quality Management System (QMS) for Team Corporate, Product and Service Line, Engineering and Manufacturing, and Operations. Global Director of Quality is responsible for operating on a cost-effective basis within the framework of company approved policies, objectives, and budgets.
  
  
**Essential Job Functions**

* Maintains a safe, secure and healthy environment by adhering to Company/Customer safety and quality standards and practices and to legal regulations, alerting others regarding potential hazards or concern
* Adheres to and is a champion of TEAM’s Core Values
* Establish a continuous improvement culture across the enterprise utilizing known methods and concepts such as Lean, Six Sigma, FMEA, Kaizen, Poka-yoke, CAPA, 8D, etc.
* Maintains contact with district, division and corporate levels to promote and instill a “Quality Culture” throughout the organization.
* Ensure TEAMs QMS is globally consistent and regionally precise based on local requirements.
* When necessary, provide training to affected personnel, including customers, to obtain maximum process efficiency, productivity, cooperation, and morale.
* Leads the Enterprise management review to evaluate quality objectives, assess the adequacy and effectiveness and continuing suitability of the existing QMS and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the Supplier Quality Management program and supports third-party and Customer assessments.
* Ensures company-wide targets and objectives are established and action plans are developed and tracked to achieve them.
* Development and implementation of performance monitoring and measurement system of leading and lagging KPIs to evaluate performance across the entire supply chain – Supplier – Order Intake - Engineering – Manufacturing – Installation – Service – Warranty.
* Development and implementation of system of associating and tracking non-conformances with costs for supplier claims, internal issues and customer escapes. This includes understanding the company’s Cost of Poor Quality and Non-Conformance Costs.
* Stay up-to-date on industry trends, including Quality-related initiatives.
* Develops medium to long-term operating strategies and recommendations for plans and programs for increasing TEAM’s Quality performance.
* Prepare capital expense and operating budgets and ensure cost-effective departmental operations.
* Support sales efforts when necessary, including the completion of pre-qualification surveys and submission of controlled quality documents to customer representatives.
* Have a general understanding of all company products and services that are available to our customers, and how TEAM’s Quality program applies to these areas.
* Ensures the Enterprise external certifications (ISO-9001, Nuclear, Aerospace, etc.) are maintained.
* Other duties as assigned

**Job Qualifications**

* Requires a bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field. Master’s degree preferred. Continuous Improvement Methodology certifications such as Six Sigma is preferred.
* Experience in Oil and Gas, Lean Manufacturing, Petrochemical, or a Field Service Industry is a must.
* 15 years’ experience in Quality or Operational Excellence related function.
* Experience with problem solving methods such as A3, FMEA, etc. preferred.
* Experience in introducing/implementing a solid warranty tracking system that captures accurate Customer and or Field related issues.

records.title: Director Quality, Institutional
records.description:
As
**Quality Director**
, you will lead the Global & NA Institutional Quality Pillar within Ecolab's future-state Global Quality organization, setting and sustaining the standards that govern product quality across the manufacturing, warehousing and distribution network. You will be responsible for building a best-in-class quality function focused on product safety, regulatory compliance, continuous improvement and a superior customer experience. Reporting to the Vice President, Global Quality, you will have primary responsibility for the North America quality management system, supplier and contract manufacturer quality, and customer complaint resolution. You will partner closely with Central Quality, Global Supplier Quality, business-aligned Quality pillars, Supply Chain, Commercial, RD&E, manufacturing, suppliers, third-party manufacturers and regulatory bodies to establish clear accountability, consistent standards, timely escalation and shared learning across the enterprise. Innovation and data-driven decision-making will be essential to activating the future-state operating model, strengthening local execution and continually increasing the value Quality delivers to the business and customers.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Own the North America quality strategy and roadmap, aligning regional priorities with the global quality agenda and future-state Global Quality operating model while driving synergies across the function
* Provide leadership and vision to the NA quality team across manufacturing plants, warehouses, and contract manufacturing partners, developing both people and technology to elevate overall performance
* Own and continuously improve the quality management system, ensuring readiness for internal, customer, regulatory and third-party audits
* Ensure compliance with FDA, EPA, ISO 9001 and other applicable regulatory and customer requirements across all North America sites
* Own the NA quality budget and cost of poor quality, including target setting for divisions
* Drive reduction in customer complaints, non-conformances and rework through structured root cause analysis and disciplined corrective and preventive action
* Establish quality metrics and reporting, using data and analytics to identify trends and direct resources to the highest-impact issues
* Partner with RD&E and the divisions on new product introductions, formula changes and specification management so that quality is designed in from the start
* Partner with the supplier and contract manufacturing teams to establish strong quality programs, including qualification, performance monitoring, audits and corrective action
* Direct the investigation and resolution of significant quality events, including product holds, recalls and customer escalations
* Build strong, trust-based relationships with commercial leaders to constantly drive improvements and efficiencies across the supply chain
* Drive standardization of quality processes across the network while implementing operational excellence and continuous improvement initiatives
* Protect Ecolab's brand by ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, and promoting environmental responsibility
* Activate the future-state Global Quality operating model across North America by clarifying decision rights, governance, interfaces, support channels and escalation paths while keeping Quality closely connected to sites, businesses and customers
* Build a connected One Quality culture by applying common standards and metrics, sharing expertise and learning across Quality pillars, and strengthening early risk visibility and consistent execution across the network
* Promote Ecolab's values and performance-based culture of excellence by demonstrating transformational leadership, and attracting, engaging, developing and rewarding the best talent in the industry

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in chemistry, engineering, supply chain or a related technical field
* 10 years of experience in quality, manufacturing or supply chain, including quality team leadership experience
* Experience owning a quality management system and regulatory compliance in a manufacturing environment
* Ability to travel up to 30% of the time

**Preferred Qualifications**

* MBA or master's degree in a technical discipline
* ASQ certification (CQE, CQA or CQM/OE) or Six Sigma Black Belt
* Large, global matrixed organization experience
* Experience in FDA, EPA and ISO 9001 regulated manufacturing environments
* Experience driving transformation through operational excellence and continuous improvement
* Strong communication skills, with ability to influence at all levels
* Track record of strong results delivery and people development
* Strategic thinking with the big picture in mind, keeping a pulse on external market factors, trends
* Ability to translate broad corporate strategies into clear, specific goals and plans

**Annual Or Hourly Compensation Range**
The base salary range for this position is $187,400.00 - $281,000.00. This position is eligible for annual bonus and long-term incentives based on performance, per plan terms. Many factors are taken into consideration when determining compensation, such as experience, education, training, geography, etc. We comply with all minimum wage and overtime laws.
  
  
**Benefits**
Ecolab strives to provide comprehensive and market-competitive benefits to meet the needs of our associates and their families. Click here to see our benefits.
  
  
*If you are viewing this posting on a site other than our Ecolab Career website, view our benefits at jobs.ecolab.com/working-here.*
**Potential Customer Requirements Notice**
To meet customer requirements and comply with local or state regulations, applicants for certain customer-facing roles may need to:
  
  

* Undergo additional background screens and/or drug/alcohol testing for customer credentialing.

**Americans With Disabilities Act (ADA)**
Ecolab will provide reasonable accommodation (such as a qualified sign language interpreter or other personal assistance) with our application process upon request as required to comply with applicable laws. If you have a disability and require accommodation assistance in this application process, please visit the Recruiting Support link in the footer of each page of our career website.
  
  
**Our Commitment to a Culture of Inclusion & Belonging**

records.description:
Elevate is committed to providing the highest quality commercial roofing, wall and lining systems to solve our customers’ challenges, grounded by a 45-year legacy of proven experience. Our mission is to deliver solutions that save time, perform reliably and protect our communities. We are devoted to building partnerships rooted in trust in reflection of our Elevate promise that Nobody Covers You Better™.
  
  
Elevate is part of the Amrize family of brands. Visit ElevateCommercialBP.com to learn more.
  
  
We’re seeking a Director of Quality Assurance who’s ready to be part of a people-first company offering best-in-class products, exceptional training, and deep industry pride—all built to help our partners and team succeed.
  
  
**About The Role**
The Quality Assurance Director strategically leads the development, implementation, and maintenance of comprehensive quality evaluation and control systems across the organization. This includes overseeing the design and analysis of inspection and testing processes, ensuring the precision and accuracy of products and equipment, driving root cause analysis for incidents, and establishing compliance with reliability standards and documentation requirements to uphold the highest levels of product quality and operational excellence
  
  
**What You'll Accomplish**

* Strategic Oversight - Overseeing and directing the overall operations of quality assurance within a company to ensure continuous improvement and compliance. This involves defining and promoting a quality mindset across the entire company.
* Quality Management System - Developing and implementing quality management systems to ensure product and service quality, and maintaining and improving quality standards, policies, and procedures.
* Compliance & Regulatory Oversight - Ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulations, and company policies, and coordinating with regulatory bodies and external auditors.
* Quality Control, Claim Mgmt, Supplier Quality - Overseeing quality control processes to ensure products meet quality standards, and conducting regular quality audits and inspections to identify and address quality issues.This also includes establishing and enforcing quality standards, testing materials and products, and developing raw material and in-process product inspection standards.
* Continuous Improvement - Leading continuous improvement initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency, and implementing best practices to reduce defects and improve processes. This can involve applying tools such as CAPA, SPC charts, Root Cause Analysis, and FMEA, and leading Six Sigma or Lean initiatives.
* Leadership & Team Development - Leading and mentoring the quality assurance team, fostering a culture of high performance and professional development, and ensuring the team has the necessary skills and resources. Responsible for generating a culture of collaboration across the organization.
* Budget & Financial Management - Achieving financial objectives by preparing the quality assurance budget, scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions.
* Customer Experience - Gathering customer feedback through gemba and data collection on quality andperformance, ensuring products meet or exceed customer expectations, and implementing changes based on feedback
* Demonstrate a commitment to communicating, improving and adhering to health, safety and environmental policies in all work environments and areas.
* Promote a culture of safety and exhibit these behaviors.

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Mgmt, or related discipline from an accredited university or college.
* At least 8 y+ years of relevant quality, continuous improvement, manufacturing experience including at least 5 years management or direct/indirect leadership experience.
* 3+ years of QMS / ISO9001 or similar experience required.
* CMQ/QE, CQE, CQA are all preferred.
* Six Sigma certification preferred.

**Additional Requirements**

* Successful candidates must adhere to all safety protocols and proper use of Amrize approved Personal Protection Equipment ("PPE"), including but not limited to respirators.
* Employees that are required to wear respirators must be clean shaven where the respirator seal meets the face in order to pass the qualitative and quantitative fit tests.

* Competitive salary
* Retirement Savings: Choose from 401(k) pre-tax and/or Roth after-tax savings

* Medical, Dental, Disability and Life Insurance
* Holistic Health & Well-being programs
* Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) & Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) for health and dependent care
* Vision and other Voluntary benefits and discounts
* Paid time off & paid holidays
* Paid Parental Leave (maternity & paternity)
* Educational Assistance Program

The Director of Quality will ensure that the site is inspection ready at all times, manage and facilitate site audits and inspections, lead execution of commitments to regulators, and ensure that quality and/or compliance issues are corrected in a timely manner. This position is the default Quality Management Representative for the Bartlett campus and reports dotted line to Top Management at the Bartlett campus.

**Description**
The
**Director of Quality & Compliance**
is responsible for leading LOPA’s overall quality strategy, overseeing the agency’s Quality Management System (QMS) and ensuring that all products, services, and internal processes meet or exceed internal and external customer expectations and regulatory standards. Reporting to the Chief Strategy Officer, the position partners with operational leaders to translate requirements and quality findings into effective, measurable practices, fostering an agency-wide culture of integrity and operational excellence.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
**Quality Strategy & QMS Governance**

* Quality Management System. Own, maintain, and continuously improve the agency-wide QMS aligning objectives with organizational priorities and applicable standards.
* Program Implementation. Lead implementation and standardization of quality initiatives, establish milestones and accountabilities, monitor adoption, and assess ongoing effectiveness and sustainability.
* Policies. Oversee agency-wide development, implementation, including version control, approval workflows for all controlled documents. Support operational owners on content development and enforcement of policies and procedures.

**Regulatory Compliance & Audits**

* Compliance Oversight. Monitor compliance with applicable CMS requirements, OPTN policies and FDA regulations and other relevant industry standards and local and federal government regulations.
* Audit Readiness and Management. Oversee internal quality audits of donation and business processes to ensure regulatory and policy compliance, leveraging operational data to advise internal stakeholders on corrective actions; ensure ongoing monitoring of implemented changes to assess long-term effectiveness and sustainability. Serve as the primary liaison during external regulatory inspections and customer audits. Oversee agency’s response to any findings or observations from external audit.
* Quality records. Ensure quality records and compliance documentation are accurate, controlled, retrievable and inspection ready.

**Continuous Improvement & CAPA**

* Root-Cause Analysis. Oversees LOPA’s Occurrence Management Program to investigate instances of procedural non-conformance, resolve systemic issues, and prevent recurrence.
* Data and KPIs. Establish quality metrics, track key performance indicators (KPIs), and analyze statistical trends to identify efficiency gains within the QMS.
* Support Process Optimization. Partner with Operations leadership and the Performance Excellence team to embed quality and drive excellence in all process improvement initiatives.

**Leadership & Supplier Management**

* Team Development. Recruit, coach develop and evaluate a team of auditors and quality team members by setting priorities and performance expectations.
* Supplier Quality. Oversee vendor qualification, auditing, and performance monitoring to ensure specifications are met.
* Customer Relations. Collaborate directly with customers to resolve quality complaints, review technical specifications, and improve satisfaction.
* Escalation: Promptly communicates significant quality or regulatory concerns to CSO and recommend protective or corrective measures.

**Requirements**
**Degree.**
Bachelor’s degree in Quality Management, Life Sciences, Public Health, Business, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
  
  
**Experience.**
Minimum of five (5) years of progressive experience in quality management, assurance and/or control, regulatory compliance, auditing or related functions within a highly regulated environment, including at least two (2) years of supervisor, management or demonstrated functional leadership experience.
  
  
**Implementation Experience.**
Demonstrated experience implementing, managing or enhancing quality management systems, regulatory compliance programs, or organization quality initiatives required.
  
  
**Industry Background.**
Proven track record of applying knowledge of the principles of quality assurance/quality control. Experience within healthcare or donation and transplantation preferred.
  
  
**Skills & Certifications.**
Certified Quality Manager (ASQ CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Black Belt, or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA) strongly preferred.
  
  
**Technical Expertise.**
Deep working knowledge of senior leadership of a Quality System. Experience applying CMS, OPTN, and FDA standards and regulations preferred.
  
  
**Leadership.**
Exceptional cross-functional communication, strong decision making and problem-solving capabilities; analytical thinker with keen ability to resolve conflict and influence executive stakeholders, adept at managing agency-wide change.

records.title: Vice President, Quality
records.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.
  
  
The Vice President of Quality is an enterprise leadership role accountable for enterprise quality performance, not just quality systems. This leader will define and execute nVent’s quality strategy across the full value chain, with direct accountability for improving customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality performance, warranty performance, product reliability, on-time-to-customer impact, and launch quality. The role will shift quality from a primarily compliance- and governance-centered function to a performance-driving enterprise capability that improves customer outcomes, operational execution, and business growth.
  
  
Reporting to the Chief Supply Chain Officer, the Vice President Quality will serve as the senior-most quality leader for nVent, setting the vision, operating model, performance expectations, capabilities, and accountability mechanisms required to scale quality as nVent grows. This leader will partner closely with segment presidents, operations, engineering, product management, sourcing and procurement, digital, commercial, legal, and finance leaders to embed quality into business decision-making and deliver measurable improvements in customer experience, reliability, warranty, launch readiness, supplier performance, operational quality, and quality-related business risk.
  
  
**What You Will Experience In This Position**
Enterprise Quality Performance and Accountability
  
  

* Own enterprise quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, launch quality, and the impact of quality issues on on-time-to-customer performance.
* Translate quality strategy into measurable business results, ensuring quality priorities are directly connected to customer experience, operational performance, growth, profitability, and risk reduction.
* Establish clear enterprise, segment, region, business unit, and site-level accountability for the quality metrics that matter most to customers and the business.
* Lead operating reviews that move beyond reporting activity to identifying performance gaps, driving root cause ownership, and sustaining measurable improvement.

New Product Quality and Launch Excellence
  
  

* Elevate new product quality as a core enterprise capability, ensuring quality is designed into high-growth platforms, strategic programs, and critical infrastructure solutions from concept through launch and field performance.
* Partner with engineering, product management, operations, and commercial leaders to strengthen quality planning, design validation, process validation, risk assessment, reliability requirements, and launch readiness across major programs such as Saturn, Avatar, Data Solutions growth initiatives, and other strategic launches.
* Ensure robust NPI quality gates, readiness reviews, and escalation criteria are in place to prevent launch defects, customer escapes, warranty exposure, and reliability issues.
* Build feedback loops from field performance, warranty, customer quality, and manufacturing quality data into product development and launch processes.

Digital Quality, Analytics, and Enterprise Quality Intelligence
  
  

* Lead the evolution of digital quality as an enterprise capability, including predictive quality, AI-enabled risk detection, manufacturing quality analytics, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
* Partner with Digital and Integrated Supply Chain leaders to modernize eQMS capabilities, automate quality workflows, strengthen data integrity, and establish a single source of truth for enterprise quality performance.
* Use advanced analytics to identify leading indicators of quality risk across product design, suppliers, manufacturing processes, field performance, warranty, and customer experience.
* Move the organization from lagging quality reporting to predictive and preventive insights that enable faster decisions, better prioritization, and measurable performance improvement.

Quality Management Systems, Compliance, and Standards
  
  

* Lead the modernization, standardization, and continuous improvement of nVent’s Quality Management System, ensuring systems and standards enable performance improvement rather than becoming ends in themselves.
* Ensure readiness and sustained compliance with applicable quality and regulatory standards, including ISO 9001 and other business-relevant standards such as ISO 14001, AS9100, customer-specific requirements, and regional regulatory expectations.
* Strengthen management review, internal audit, external audit, and corrective and preventive action processes to ensure systemic issues are identified, resolved, and prevented from recurring.
* Partner with legal, compliance, engineering, operations, and commercial teams to manage quality-related risk and ensure quality commitments are understood, objective, and executable.

Customer, Supplier, and Operational Quality
  
  

* Build customer quality capability that improves responsiveness, transparency, containment, corrective action effectiveness, customer confidence, and reduction of repeat escapes.
* Advance supplier quality strategy, qualification, audit discipline, scorecards, supplier development, and escalation processes to improve supplier performance and protect customer commitments.
* Embed quality into manufacturing and operational processes with a focus on defect prevention, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, error proofing, and flow to customer.
* Use customer feedback, warranty data, supplier performance, manufacturing quality, field performance, and operational metrics to prioritize systemic improvement opportunities.

Leadership, Talent, and Quality Culture
  
  

* Champion a quality-first culture where leaders model prevention-based decision-making and teams are empowered to stop, escalate, and resolve issues before they reach the customer.
* Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing quality leadership team with clear accountability, succession depth, and strong capability across enterprise, segment, regional, and site quality roles.
* Lead through influence in a matrixed environment, balancing enterprise standards with business-specific execution needs and measurable performance outcomes.
* Model executive leadership behaviors, including strategic thinking, courageous decision-making, stakeholder engagement, talent development, collaboration, adaptability, and self-accountability.

**You Have**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive quality, operations, engineering, or supply chain leadership experience in a global manufacturing environment, including significant leadership of multi-site or enterprise quality functions.
* Demonstrated experience improving quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, and launch quality.
* Strong experience in new product quality, design validation, process validation, launch readiness, reliability engineering, and quality risk management for complex product portfolios.
* Experience advancing digital quality capabilities, including eQMS, quality analytics, digital traceability, predictive insights, and AI-enabled risk detection.
* Proven ability to lead enterprise-level change across a complex, matrixed, global organization.
* Exceptional communication, influencing, and executive presence, with the ability to translate quality priorities into business value.
* Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.

**Suggested Success Measures**

* Reduced customer escapes and repeat quality issues, with improved containment, responsiveness, and corrective action effectiveness.
* Improved cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, warranty performance, and on-time-to-customer impact from quality issues.
* Improved supplier quality performance through stronger qualification, development, governance, scorecards, and corrective action discipline.
* Stronger new product quality outcomes, including improved launch readiness, fewer launch defects, reduced warranty exposure, and better reliability performance.
* Expanded digital quality maturity, including predictive quality insights, AI-enabled risk detection, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
* Increased quality maturity from reactive issue management to proactive prevention, measurable performance improvement, and stronger enterprise accountability.

**We Have**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day

+ nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
+ Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.

* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work

+ We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
+ Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

- Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

* Innovative & adaptable
* Dedicated to absolute integrity
* Focused on the customer first
* Respectful and team oriented
* Optimistic and energizing
* Accountable for performance
* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency**
nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance.
