records.description:
**Responsibilities**
****Position Summary****
The Director of Operational Excellence & Assurance owns two closely linked functions at Related Digital: driving continuous improvement across data center operations, and independently assessing and auditing operational, safety, and quality performance against the Related Digital EHS Program Manual, site standard operating procedures, and applicable regulatory and industry standards. This includes auditing facility management partner performance against contractual SLAs and KPIs, and supporting Related Digital’s SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certification programs. This role designs and executes the internal audit and assessment program, verifies that field practice matches documented procedure, drives corrective action to closure, and partners with site and regional leadership to convert audit findings into lasting process improvement. The role carries Stop Work Authority and reports significant findings directly to site and operations leadership.
  
  
****Key Responsibilities****
****Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement****

* Lead site and portfolio level continuous improvement initiatives to improve the safety, reliability, quality, and efficiency of data center operations.
* Establish and maintain standardized operating procedures, playbooks, and best-practice sharing across sites.
* Define, track, and report key performance indicators (KPIs) for operational performance, safety, and compliance; identify trends and improvement opportunities.
* Facilitate root cause analysis and corrective/preventive action (CAPA) processes for operational, safety, and quality events, consistent with the Incident Investigation & Root Cause Analysis Program.
* Partner with Engineering, Facilities, and EHS teams to standardize processes across the portfolio and support new site commissioning and operational readiness.
* Champion a culture of continuous improvement, change management, and operational discipline among site teams.
* Monitor energy performance, including PUE, against site design targets and drive corrective action for deviations.

****Operational Assessment & Internal Audit****

* Design, own, and execute the annual internal audit and operational assessment plan across all Related Digital sites, covering all EHS programs, life-safety systems, critical facility operations, and quality/process compliance.
* Conduct on-site operational assessments and compliance audits against the Program Manuals, site SOPs, inspection/checklist templates, and applicable regulatory or industry standards (OSHA, NFPA, ANSI, Uptime Institute Tier Standards, SOC2, ISO 9001/45001/14001).
* Evaluate the completeness and currency of site-level checklists, inspection logs, JHAs/AHAs, and training records against the EHS Training Requirements Matrix.
* Document audit findings, assign risk ratings, and issue formal assessment reports to site and regional leadership.
* Track corrective action plans (CAPs) to closure, verifying effectiveness through follow-up audits.
* Maintain audit program documentation, evidence, and records consistent with the Records Management & Retention Program.
* Support external audits, customer/tenant due-diligence assessments, and regulatory inspections as the internal subject matter expert.
* Audit physical security programs, covering access control, credentialing, and key management.
* Audit commissioning and construction documentation, such as MOPs, RCAs, and general contractor turnover packages, for completeness before closeout.

****Facility Management Partner & Vendor Oversight****

* Audit facility management partner performance against contractual SLAs and KPIs, covering maintenance completion, staffing, and site inspections; validate SLA credits using EPMS, BMS, CMMS, and incident log data.
* Audit facility management partner Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery programs, and verify adherence to change management and work notification protocols.
* Support evaluation of facility management partner RFP responses and subcontractor compliance.
* Review partner markups, pricing transparency, and preferred vendor compliance.
* Support transition and exit audits when facility management partners change.

****Governance, Training & Reporting****

* Maintain and continuously improve the internal audit methodology, scoring rubrics, and assessment tools.
* Deliver periodic (e.g., quarterly) operational excellence and audit performance reporting to executive leadership, including site scorecards and trend analysis.
* Partner with the Site EHS Manager and Safety Training Program owners to close training and competency gaps identified during assessments.
* Provide coaching and calibration to site leadership on self-assessment practices, audit readiness, and continuous improvement tools.
* Participate in incident investigation reviews where root causes point to systemic operational or procedural gaps.
* Lead Related Digital’s SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 audit cycles, including evidence collection and coordination with external auditors.
* Review facility management partner SOC 2 and ISO 27001 attestation reports where relevant to Related Digital’s compliance obligations.

**Qualifications**
****Educational and Certifications****
**Minimum Education (Required):**

* Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Occupational Safety & Health, Business Administration, Operations Management, Quality Management, or another related technical or business discipline.
* Equivalent experience in lieu of degree: an Associate’s degree plus a minimum of four (4) additional years of directly relevant operational excellence, quality assurance, or internal audit experience, or a high school diploma/GED plus eight (8) years of directly relevant experience, may be considered in place of the bachelor’s degree requirement.

**Preferred Education:**

* Master’s degree in Business Administration (MBA), Engineering Management, Occupational Safety, Quality Systems, or a related field.
* Formal coursework or certificate training in Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or internal audit methodology.

**Required and Preferred Certifications:**

* OSHA 30-Hour General Industry or Construction certification.
* Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), or CISA.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt.
* Certified Safety Professional (CSP), Associate Safety Professional (ASP), or Certified Industrial Hygienist (CIH).
* Data center industry certification (e.g., CDCP/CDCS/CDCE, CDCAP, or Uptime Institute Accredited Tier Specialist).

****Experience****

* Minimum 7–10 years of progressive experience in operations, quality assurance, EHS, or internal audit roles.
* At least 3 years of that experience in a data center, other critical facility, manufacturing, or industrial operating environment.
* Minimum 3 years leading or managing an internal audit, quality assurance, or operational assessment program.
* Demonstrated track record designing and executing continuous improvement initiatives with measurable, documented results.
* Experience auditing against OSHA/ANSI/NFPA standards, SOC, ISO 9001/45001/14001, IATF 16949, or Uptime Institute Tier Standards is strongly preferred given the mission-critical facility environment.
* Supervisory or project leadership experience, including leading cross-functional teams without direct authority.

****Skills & Core Competencies****

* Strong analytical and root-cause problem-solving skills; able to synthesize audit data into clear, actionable insights.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to present findings to site staff, peers, and executive leadership with equal clarity.
* High attention to detail balanced with pragmatic judgment on risk prioritization.
* Proficiency with audit/GRC software, statistical and process tools (e.g., Minitab, Excel), and data visualization tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) is a plus.
* Comfortable exercising Stop Work Authority and holding site teams accountable with professionalism and tact.
* Working knowledge of critical facility systems (electrical, mechanical, fire/life safety) is preferred.
* Self-directed, able to plan and manage a multi-site audit calendar with minimal oversight.

****Work Environment & Physical Demands****

* Ability to walk extended distances across large facility footprints, climb stairs and ladders, and work in mechanical/electrical rooms with variable noise and temperature.
* Occasional lifting of up to 25 lbs.
* Ability to sit, stand, and use a computer for extended periods when preparing audit reports and analysis.

****Travel Requirements****

* Up to 40–50% domestic travel across the Related Digital site portfolio can be required, including occasional multi-day site visits. A valid driver’s license is required; ability to travel by air and a US passport is required.

**Overview**
**Why Related Digital?**
Formed in 1972, Related is the most prominent privately-owned real estate firm in the United States. Headquartered in New York City, the company has offices and major developments across the world. Related owns and manages a premier portfolio of assets valued at over $70 billion, including the 28-acre Hudson Yards neighborhood on Manhattan’s West Side.
  
  
Related believes in investing in its talent and cultivates a positive, team-oriented environment where every voice is valued. Employees are encouraged to boldly take on new challenges, transcend the status quo, and demonstrate strong entrepreneurial spirit. In its relentless commitment to excellence, Related fosters an innovative approach so that team members can positively impact the communities in which they conduct business.
  
  
Founded by Related Companies, Related Digital is a leading vertically integrated data center development and investment platform that partners with leading technology companies to provide best-in-class digital infrastructure and holistic energy solutions through responsible, community-centered development. Related Digital currently has $55B in active data center development and construction underway representing 6GW of capacity, with projects in Ontario, Wyoming, Michigan, Missouri, Illinois and Texas.
  
  
Its vertically integrated platform encompasses site acquisition, entitlements, supply chain procurement, steel fabrication, construction management, and utility-scale energy solutions, providing hyperscalers with differentiated, end-to-end execution. Learn more at related-digital.com .
  
  
For information about how we use your personal information, including information submitted for career opportunities, please review our Privacy Policy at https://www.related.com/privacy-policy .

**POSITION SUMMARY:**

Operating as a true leader of leaders, this role drives a unified quality and safety culture and holds ultimate responsibility for the Quality Management System (QMS).

The Director executes the quality strategy by leading a comprehensive team of specialized quality managers responsible for Supplier Quality, Customer Quality, Production Quality (OEM), Repair Station Quality as well as inspection and NDT. This position serves as the primary leadership focal point to large commercial aerospace customers, critical suppliers, regulatory agencies, and group/corporate leadership.

Reports directly to the Division General Manager and is a member of the division leadership team, with a strong dotted line to the VP of Quality.

* Oversees the effective documentation and implementation of the quality management system to assure compliance with customer and regulatory requirements and the standards set by corporate/division policies.
* Works with Division leadership to ensure that individuals performing functions affecting quality are trained and demonstrate the appropriate skills and performance results.
* Coordinates necessary team member resources for internal, customer and third-party quality system audits.
* Maintains a corrective action system to analyze and correct nonconforming conditions and complaints.
* Implements the performance measurements necessary to effectively evaluate organizational performance and trends in product quality, services, customer satisfaction and the cost of poor quality. Uses the results of performance evaluation to target improvement efforts.
* Collaborates with the supply chain function on the development and implementation of a supplier management strategy.
* Assess supplier capabilities and monitor supplier quality to ensure desired levels of performance.
* Collaborates with Engineering on new product development and design review for quality/reliability issues.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

* Bachelor's Degree in an Engineering or related technical/scientific discipline. An M.B.A., or an advanced technical degree is strongly preferred.
* 10+ years leading a large quality department within the aerospace or automotive manufacturing industry.
* Thorough knowledge of Standard AS9100 Quality Management Systems.

**Compensation Range**

$240,000 - $280,000 / Year

**Overview**

**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!** Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our Bakery business, lead great people, and strengthen the systems behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests have loved for decades.

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to the Bakery President and executive leadership, providing clear perspective on food safety and quality risks, audit readiness, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Ensure trust and confidence in the function through technical credibility, transparency, strong partnerships, and consistent execution.
* Strengthen compliance and operational discipline across GMPs, HACCP, SQF, AIB, sanitation, allergen controls, environmental monitoring, traceability, supplier quality, microbiological testing, and recall readiness.
* Establish sustained audit readiness and ensure findings have clear ownership, effective corrective actions, and lasting resolution.
* Ensure highly systematic and disciplined adherence to product and process standards on a real-time basis to guarantee our cakes are beautiful and delicious.
* Build greater rigor around root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, addressing systemic issues rather than symptoms.
* Provide leadership across product and process quality, customer complaints, foreign-material controls, product holds, specifications, labeling, formulas, recipes, and Technical Services.
* Establish meaningful metrics and use data to identify trends, prioritize risk, and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Lead significant food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory matters with urgency, sound judgment, and appropriate escalation.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, and Technical Services organization with the talent and capabilities needed for long-term success.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Research and Development, and Human Resources to strengthen ownership and accountability for food safety and quality across the business.
* Prioritize resources and investments against the greatest risks and opportunities while effectively managing the function’s budget.

**Qualifications**

* 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, or Technical Services within food manufacturing, including senior-level, multi-site responsibility.
* Demonstrated success leading food safety and quality strategy, organizational transformation, culture improvement, and high-performing technical teams.
* Deep expertise in GMPs, HACCP, preventive controls, sanitation, microbiological risk, allergen management, environmental monitoring, traceability, recalls, supplier quality, AIB, SQF, and food safety management systems.
* Extensive experience leading regulatory, certification, customer, and internal audits from preparation through corrective action and sustainable closure.
* Expertise in root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, risk assessment, and incident investigation.
* Proven ability to build organizational trust, strengthen accountability, influence senior leaders, and lead through significant change.
* Bachelor’s degree in microbiology, chemistry, food science, food safety, biology, engineering, or a closely related discipline.

**What we prefer:**

  

* Leadership experience within the bakery or dessert industry; experience in similarly complex food-manufacturing environments will also be considered.
* Master’s degree in a related technical or business discipline.
* Relevant certifications such as SQF Practitioner, HACCP, PCQI, or Certified Food Scientist.
* Bilingual English/Spanish.

**Meet Vestis®:** For the People Who Make It All Work
  
At Vestis®, we provide uniforms, workplace supplies, and professional cleaning that help businesses simplify their workday and keep their teams safe, confident, and focused on what matters most. More than a provider, we are a partner in productivity, trusted to keep you running.
  
Join us and build a career supporting the people who make it all work.
  
  
Overview
  
The Vice President of Distribution Center Operations will lead the product distribution strategy and drive an economically competitive operation that delivers both best-in-class customer experience and distribution cost advantages across all facilities supporting Vestis Rental and Direct Sale customers.
  
This leader will influence and reinforce a portfolio of core values and accountability standards centered on safety, workforce engagement, customer experience, operational efficiency, and innovative solutions that support business goals. This role is responsible for deploying strategies and actionable plans that deliver measurable performance improvement.
  
This leader will also define and advance the technology roadmap for Distribution Center Operations, identifying opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence (AI), robotics, automation, advanced analytics, and other emerging technologies to improve safety, productivity, quality, service, capacity, and cost.
  
The Vice President will promote data-driven performance visibility, real-time corrective action, and strong cross-functional collaboration. This leader will work effectively with business partners to identify, address, and resolve operational issues.
  
This role will set goals and oversee key metrics related to customer fill rates, customer satisfaction, footprint utilization, inventory management, optimization and total DC cost, along with other key measures tied to Distribution Center Operations.
  
Responsibilities/Essential Functions
  

* Set and deliver the overall vision and distribution strategy for national and international distribution centers to ensure end-to-end customer needs are met at the lowest possible cost.
* Lead a high-performing team of supply chain practitioners, with direct and indirect responsibility for an organization of more than 600 employees.
* Partner with Human Resources to design and implement workforce strategies for each distribution center location, including the evolution of workforce skills needed to support increasingly automated and technology-enabled operations.
* Define objectives, establish key performance metrics, and create a regular review cadence across safety, quality, fill rate, customer satisfaction, inventory management, budget performance, and other critical operating areas.
* Implement metrics, processes, and operating routines that drive accountability and ensure results.
* Improve costs year over year through disciplined operational execution and continuous improvement.
* Drive performance improvement through the use of continuous improvement methodology.
* Build strong cross-functional partnerships to identify, escalate, and resolve operational issues and improvement opportunities.
* Set the strategic direction and oversee major projects across national and international locations, including distribution center layout changes, equipment needs, space utilization, capital expenses, major repairs, and related operational requirements.
* Manage domestic and international direct and indirect reporting teams to ensure processes and procedures are consistent across all facilities.
* Lead the annual budgeting process in partnership with DC Operations and Direct Sale Finance Teams and Sales Leadership.
* Stay current on information, technology, and trends affecting functional areas; promote innovation and make appropriate recommendations to executive leadership.
* Develop and execute a multi-year distribution technology and automation roadmap, including the evaluation and adoption of AI, robotics, material-handling automation, advanced analytics, and emerging distribution technologies where they provide measurable operational and financial value.
* Evaluate opportunities to automate manual and repetitive processes across receiving, put-away, inventory movement, picking, packing, sortation, shipping, and related distribution workflows.
* Establish business cases and success measures for major automation and technology investments, including productivity improvement, service impact, safety, capacity, labor requirements, operating cost, capital requirements, and return on investment.
* Partner with Information Technology, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, Human Resources, and external technology partners to successfully pilot, scale, and operationalize new distribution technologies across the network.
* Use data, predictive analytics, and AI-enabled decision support to improve demand and capacity planning, inventory positioning, workforce planning, asset utilization, operational visibility, and decision-making.
* Build a culture of innovation in which technology augments the workforce, improves safety and efficiency, and prepares the distribution organization for future operating requirements.
* Set the overall strategy for operational performance planning to drive quality standards and efficiency.
* Oversee and monitor safety and security in accordance with national and international requirements for facilities and employees. Ensure proper training and adherence to company requirements.
* Drive employment decisions and recommendations, including hiring, retention, improvement plans, transfers, promotions, corrective actions, terminations, and pay adjustments.
* Manage employee performance and support improvement through coaching, mentoring, and formal performance reviews.
* Recommend, plan, and implement employee training and skill development activities.
* Lead communication on company and departmental issues, priorities, and goals. Provide oversight of employee growth and development through weekly team meetings, regular one-on-one meetings, coaching, performance management, training, and company-sponsored learning opportunities.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities
  

* Demonstrated understanding of technical issues within a global distribution framework.
* Strong understanding of modern distribution technologies, including warehouse automation, robotics, AI, machine learning applications, advanced analytics, and automated material-handling solutions.
* Ability to translate emerging technology into practical operational use cases and measurable business outcomes rather than implementing technology for technology’s sake.
* Strong understanding of automation investment strategy, including business-case development, scalability, change management, operational readiness, and return on investment.
* Ability to lead transformation in environments where automated and traditional operations may need to coexist across different facilities.
* Strong project leadership and cross-functional leadership experience.
* Ability to think, plan, and execute strategically.
* Ability to influence and build consensus with executive leadership.
* Comfortable operating in ambiguity.
* Decisive and persuasive, with a strong sense of urgency and a proven ability to drive results.
* Strong organizational skills.
* Excellent analytical skills and technical capabilities.
* Willingness and ability to travel extensively, both nationally and internationally.

Role is based in Lawrenceville, GA.
  
Requires up to 50% travel across the U.S. and Canada.
  
Work includes distribution center, plant, and office environments, including corporate office interaction in Roswell, GA.
  
Must comply with all company safety, security, and site-specific requirements.
  
Experience/Qualifications
  

* 15 years of experience leading a large workforce in a high-volume, fast-paced global distribution or manufacturing network.

* Recognized thought leader and expert within business, supply chain, logistics, and/or global distribution disciplines.

---------------------

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. This role requires strong business judgment, operational discipline, technical understanding, and the ability to build an accountable, collaborative culture focused on safety, food safety, quality, service, cost, and continuous improvement.

**On-Site:** Based full-time in Charlotte, NC at Big Beverages manufacturing facility

**Travel Requirements:** Up to 25% domestic travel

**People Management Responsibilities:** Yes

**Reports To:** VP of Manufacturing

**Role Type:** Full-Time

 **Requirements**  

* **Experience:** 7-10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, preferably in high-speed beverage filling/canning, food, or consumer packaged goods operations, including at least 3–5 years leading a plant or multi-department operation with full responsibility for production performance and hourly teams.
* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, Food Science, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* Experience leading high-volume, automated manufacturing operations and managing production, maintenance, engineering, quality, safety, and continuous improvement functions.
* Working knowledge of FSSC 22000, ISO 22000 principles, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, food defense, food fraud prevention, traceability, prerequisite programs, CAPA systems, and audit readiness.
* Demonstrated success improving OEE, schedule attainment, throughput, labor efficiency, yield, waste, downtime, quality, cost performance, and equipment reliability through disciplined operating systems.
* Experience managing budgets, labor planning, capital projects, business cases, and plant-level financial performance.
* Experience hiring, developing, coaching, and leading large hourly and salaried teams, including supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Experience using ERP/MRP, MES, maintenance-management, and manufacturing-performance systems to make data-driven decisions.
* Strong analytical, communication, organization, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work onsite at the manufacturing facility and support a flexible schedule based on operational needs.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Food Science, or a related field.
* PCQI, HACCP, FSSC 22000, Lean Six Sigma, or similar certification or training.
* Hands-on experience with high-speed carbonated beverage filling and canning lines, including syrup batching/blending, water treatment, carbonation, fillers, can seamers and double-seam integrity, can warmers/pasteurizers, CIP sanitation, and end-of-line packaging and palletizing.
* Experience with plant start-ups, expansions, new line installations, automation, commissioning, scale-up, or major capital investments.
* Experience supporting a rapidly growing consumer brand or publicly traded company.
* Experience working with labor relations or represented manufacturing environments.

### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all manufacturing operations to ensure the safe, efficient, and consistent production of high-quality canned beverages from production scheduling through finished-goods handoff.
* Develop and execute the plant operating strategy in alignment with CELSIUS business objectives, demand forecasts, customer requirements, and long-term growth plans.
* Own production planning, capacity, staffing, schedule attainment, changeovers, line utilization, labor efficiency, and daily operating execution.
* Establish clear performance expectations and accountability across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, warehouse, and support functions.
* Drive key operating metrics, including safety, OEE, throughput, yield, scrap, waste, downtime, labor productivity, cost per unit, on-time production, and schedule attainment.
* Establish and sustain leader standard work, tiered accountability, visual management, root-cause problem solving, standard work, and continuous-improvement routines.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering on preventive and predictive maintenance, equipment reliability, automation, capital priorities, commissioning, line expansions, and new technology implementation.
* Coordinate with Warehousing, Logistics, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Customer Service to maintain material availability, protect product integrity, and ensure accurate and timely finished-goods handoff.
* Maintain compliance with applicable safety, environmental, food-contact, quality, food-safety, and regulatory requirements, including FSSC 22000, HACCP, GMP, FSMA, and customer standards.
* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities.
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality.
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing.
* Lead audit readiness and support certification, surveillance, recertification, customer, regulatory, internal, and third-party audits.
* Maintain a strong safety culture through employee engagement, training, audits, risk assessments, safety observations, incident investigations, emergency preparedness, and corrective-action plans.
* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce.
* Build leadership capability through coaching, performance management, individual development plans, skills matrices, cross-training, succession planning, and consistent leader standard work.
* Lead labor planning and workforce optimization in response to production volumes, seasonality, new product requirements, and business growth.
* Manage the plant operating budget, labor costs, maintenance spending, capital expenditures, and other controllable expenses.
* Analyze operational and financial data to identify trends, risks, opportunities, and actions needed to improve plant performance.
* Communicate plant performance, operating priorities, business risks, resource needs, and improvement plans clearly to plant and executive leadership.
* Contribute to network and growth planning, including capacity, new product introductions, and line additions, in partnership with corporate Operations and Supply Chain.
* Build strong working relationships with corporate brand, R&D/innovation, Quality, and Supply Chain partners, as well as co-pack customers and key suppliers where applicable.
* Promote a culture consistent with CELSIUS values, including ownership, agility, grit, commercial thinking, collaboration, positive influence, and a bias for action.
* Provide site-wide leadership that translates company goals into plant priorities, targets, and daily execution.
* Perform other duties and special projects as assigned.
* Leadership Expectations
* Lead with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
* Make thoughtful, timely decisions in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
* Balance immediate production needs with long-term operational excellence.
* Build trust across plant, corporate, commercial, and cross-functional teams.
* Develop people and create a culture where employees are engaged, respected, and empowered to perform at their best.
* Use facts, data, and business judgment to solve problems and make decisions.
* Maintain high standards for safety, food safety, quality, compliance, and operational execution.
* Be comfortable operating in a high-growth consumer products environment where priorities may change quickly.

### **Physical Demands and Work Environment**

This role is based on the manufacturing floor and in plant offices. The work environment includes high-speed automated equipment, elevated noise levels requiring hearing protection, wet floors, temperature variation, and forklift traffic. Required PPE (such as safety glasses, hearing protection, and safety footwear) must be worn in production areas, and all plant safety, GMP, and food-safety rules must be followed. The role regularly requires standing and walking for extended periods and climbing stairs and platforms, and occasionally lifting up to 25 pounds. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

 **Benefits**  

* Comprehensive Medical, Dental & Vision benefits
* Long- and short-term disability
* Life insurance
* 10 Vacation days per year, subject to accrual policy
* 11 Company paid holidays
* 401(k) with Company match
* Identity theft and legal services

*The base salary range for this position is dependent on experience and location. The final offer will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, and qualifications. This position may be eligible for other compensation, including bonuses and Restricted Stock Units (subject to company plans).*

*We promptly review all applications. Highly qualified candidates will be contacted for interviews.*

*CELSIUS Holdings, Inc. celebrates diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We provide equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all applicants without regard to race, color, ethnicity, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability status, veteran status, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws. If you require accommodations during the application process, please reach out to* *careers@celsius.com**.*

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job.*

records.title: Director, Advanced Hardware Manufacturing
records.description:
Every Zoox vehicle depends on the electronic and sensor hardware our Advanced Hardware Manufacturing team builds and tests. As Director, you will lead the organization that takes this hardware from early builds to serial volume, helping bring safer, cleaner mobility to cities.

Our team values safety first, ownership, and learning together. We solve problems in the open and improve how we work every day. You will be part of the Manufacturing Operations leadership team, reporting to the Vice President of Manufacturing Operations. You will partner closely with Hardware Engineering, Test Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Logistics, Environmental Health and Safety (EHS), and Program Management. This role offers room to grow as our production footprint and team expand.

### **In this role, you will:**

* Lead daily operations of advanced hardware assembly and test lines across multiple shifts, delivering on safety, quality, delivery, and cost, and build a culture that puts people and product safety first.
* Turn the vehicle demand plan into production and capacity plans covering labor, equipment, shifts, and yield, and lead expansion into new lines and areas with Equipment Engineering and Facilities.
* Improve first pass yield and process capability through standardized processes, and partner cross-functionally on root cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Manage the Advanced Hardware Laboratories to support R&D across the sensors and compute domains. Lead the build, testing, and pilot production of early-stage prototypes, maturing technical solutions for seamless transition to high-volume manufacturing.
* Bring new products and design changes from pilot builds to volume production with Hardware and Test Engineering, giving design-for-manufacturing input early.
* Apply lean methods and structured problem solving, and run a data-driven operating rhythm on delivery, cycle time, yield, utilization, and unit cost.
* Own operating, capital, and headcount budgets, and deliver cost reduction roadmaps.
* Hire, develop, and retain managers, supervisors, line leads, and technicians, with succession and training plans that support multi-shift operations.

### **Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Management, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* At least 15 years in manufacturing operations for complex electronic or sensor hardware, including at least 8 years leading multi-level production organizations and presenting to executive leadership.
* Experience taking hardware products from new product introduction through ramp to serial production.
* Results improving safety, quality, delivery, and cost through lean manufacturing and structured problem solving.
* Experience owning operating, capital, and headcount budgets, including investments in production lines or facilities.

### **Bonus Qualifications**

* Experience standing up new production lines or facilities in a high-growth environment.
* Experience with electronics assembly and automated test, including ESD control and end-of-line test.
* Familiarity with manufacturing execution, ERP, and quality management systems, and standards such as ISO 9001 or IATF 16949.

There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.

Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

records.title: Director of Offsite Production - Fabrication
records.description:
**At ACI we build our company and our culture not by counting people, but by making our people count!**

Atlantic Constructors is seeking dynamic, motivated, career minded individuals to join our expanding team! Atlantic Constructors has been recognized as an industry leader in the Mid-Atlantic Region for over 50 years.

**Benefits:**

* ***$0.00 COST FOR MEDICAL, DENTAL, SHORT TERM DISABILITYLIFE INSURANCE (EMPLOYEE ONLY) COVERAGE!***
* Dental Insurance Plan
* Vision Insurance Plan
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with Generous Company Matching
* Health Savings Plan with Generous Company Matching
* Wellness Programs

Atlantic Constructors offers competitive benefits, for more information check out our comprehensive list on our website. ACIBuilds.com

**Role Overview:**
==================

The Director of Offsite Production is responsible for the leadership, performance, and continued growth of offsite production across company facilities. The role oversees carbon and stainless steel pipe fabrication and non-volumetric prefabrication and manufacturing, including pipe racks, equipment skids, supports, frames, and multi-trade assemblies. The Director establishes the operating systems, production standards, capacity, and cross-functional coordination required to deliver safe, compliant, high-quality work on schedule.

This leader is accountable for implementing improvements that increase production capacity, labor productivity, throughput, and schedule reliability. The Director will implement and sustain Lean manufacturing methodologies, eliminate waste and production constraints, reduce rework, and create repeatable processes that support scalable offsite manufacturing. The position works closely with Estimating, Engineering, VDC, Procurement, Project Management, Quality, Safety, and field operations to align production with project and business objectives.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

**Offsite Production Leadership**
---------------------------------

* Provide enterprise leadership for pipe fabrication, prefabrication, and manufacturing operations across company facilities and approved external production partners.
* Translate backlog, project schedules, and sales forecasts into capacity plans, staffing requirements, production priorities, and facility needs.
* Establish a consistent operating cadence for production planning, readiness reviews, constraint management, performance reporting, and executive escalation.
* Develop scalable operating standards that support growth while maintaining safety, quality, cost control, and predictable delivery performance.
* Coordinate work across facilities to balance demand, available labor, equipment, and production capability.

**Pipe Fabrication Operations**
-------------------------------

* Direct carbon and stainless steel pipe fabrication operations, including material receiving, cutting, beveling, fit-up, welding, inspection, testing, coating coordination, staging, and shipment.
* Ensure spool sequencing, production release, shop loading, and work packaging align with approved drawings, project priorities, and field installation requirements.
* Maintain compliance with applicable codes, specifications, welding procedures, ASME and AWS requirements, customer quality plans, and company standards.
* Improve material traceability, weld documentation, inspection records, testing status, and turnover packages for fabricated systems.

**Prefabrication and Manufacturing Operations**
-----------------------------------------------

* Lead production of non-volumetric prefabricated assemblies, including pipe racks, equipment skids, structural supports, frames, and multi-trade assemblies.
* Develop repeatable production cells, workstations, tooling, fixtures, travelers, and assembly sequences that improve flow and reduce variation.
* Ensure manufacturing plans account for structural, mechanical, electrical, controls, insulation, coatings, testing, preservation, packaging, and logistics requirements, as applicable.
* Support the transition of first-of-a-kind work into stable, repeatable production through lessons learned, standardized design, and controlled process updates.

**Production Planning and Readiness**
-------------------------------------

* Establish production-readiness criteria to confirm approved drawings, bills of material, work instructions, quality requirements, tooling, materials, and labor are available before work is released.
* Partner with Engineering and VDC to improve constructability, spool and assembly breakdown, drawing release sequencing, and design for manufacturing and assembly.
* Coordinate with Procurement and material-control teams to maintain visibility to shortages, supplier commitments, receiving status, kitting, and point-of-use material availability.
* Identify production constraints early, assign recovery actions, and communicate schedule or capacity risks to Project Management and executive leadership.
* Maintain production schedules that clearly identify priorities, dependencies, resource loading, planned output, and required shipment dates.

**Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement**
-------------------------------------------------

* Lead continuous-improvement initiatives that increase production capacity, labor productivity, throughput, and schedule reliability across all offsite operations.
* Implement and sustain Lean manufacturing methodologies, including 5S, standard work, value-stream mapping, visual management, cellular production, daily tiered accountability, Kaizen events, mistake-proofing, and continuous-flow principles.
* Evaluate workflows, facility layouts, material movement, staffing, tooling, and equipment utilization to identify and eliminate bottlenecks, waste, waiting, excess handling, rework, and other non-value-added activity.
* Use time studies, cycle-time analysis, workload balancing, root-cause analysis, and structured problem-solving to improve production performance and reduce manufacturing lead time.
* Develop and maintain standard work instructions and repeatable manufacturing processes that improve safety, quality, training effectiveness, and output predictability.
* Lead initiatives to reduce setup and changeover time, control work in process, improve material flow, and increase productive labor utilization.
* Maintain an improvement pipeline with defined owners, target benefits, implementation dates, and verified results; ensure completed improvements are standardized and sustained.
* Evaluate and implement automation, machinery, software, tooling, and manufacturing technologies that improve safety, quality, efficiency, and capacity.

**Throughput Capacity and Performance Management**
--------------------------------------------------

* Establish production targets and capacity models based on takt time, cycle time, labor availability, equipment constraints, facility limits, and project demand.
* Track and improve key performance indicators such as safety performance, labor hours per spool or assembly, plan attainment, throughput, work in process, first-pass yield, rework, equipment utilization, and on-time completion and shipment.
* Develop visual dashboards and tiered performance reviews that provide timely, accurate information to supervisors, project teams, and executive leadership.
* Analyze performance gaps, determine root causes, implement corrective and preventive actions, and verify that results are sustained.
* Use production data to validate estimating assumptions, workforce plans, capital investments, and future capacity requirements.

**Supplier and External Fabrication Partner Management**
--------------------------------------------------------

* Qualify, onboard, and manage third-party fabrication and manufacturing partners when additional capacity or specialized capability is required.
* Define scopes of work, quality requirements, documentation, inspection points, schedule expectations, material responsibilities, and delivery requirements for outsourced work.
* Monitor supplier performance for safety, quality, responsiveness, cost, schedule adherence, and corrective-action closure.
* Coordinate external production with internal Engineering, Procurement, Quality, Project Management, and logistics teams.

**Estimating and Preconstruction Support**
------------------------------------------

* Support Estimating and Preconstruction with production strategies, labor assumptions, production rates, facility requirements, tooling, equipment, subcontract capacity, and logistics considerations.
* Review proposed scope, drawings, specifications, and schedules to identify production risks, constructability issues, testing requirements, and opportunities for prefabrication or standardization.
* Provide fact-based labor and throughput data to improve estimate accuracy and establish achievable production commitments.
* Participate in make-or-buy decisions and recommend the most effective production approach based on capability, capacity, cost, risk, and schedule.

**Quality Safety and Delivery**
-------------------------------

* Promote a production culture in which safety, quality, and operational discipline are built into the process and are never traded for output.
* Partner with Safety and Quality leaders to establish training, inspections, hold points, audits, nonconformance controls, and corrective-action processes.
* Ensure completed work is inspected, tested, documented, preserved, packaged, and released in accordance with project and company requirements.
* Drive reduction of defects, weld repairs, material damage, punch-list items, field rework, and incomplete turnover documentation.
* Coordinate staging, loading, transportation readiness, and shipment sequencing to support safe handling and efficient field installation.

**Team Leadership and Development**
-----------------------------------

* Build and lead an accountable organization of production managers, superintendents, supervisors, planners, coordinators, and skilled craft professionals.
* Define roles, decision rights, staffing plans, performance expectations, and development paths for the offsite production team.
* Train leaders and production personnel in Lean principles, standard work, problem-solving, root-cause analysis, visual management, and data-driven decision-making.
* Develop succession plans and cross-training programs that increase workforce flexibility and reduce dependency on single points of knowledge.
* Create a culture of ownership, urgency, teamwork, continuous improvement, and respect for people.

**Qualifications and Experience**
=================================

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, construction management, manufacturing, operations, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Ten or more years of progressive experience in fabrication, prefabrication, manufacturing, construction operations, or a closely related production environment, including significant leadership responsibility.
* Demonstrated success improving production throughput, labor productivity, quality, schedule performance, and operating discipline.
* Practical experience implementing Lean manufacturing or continuous-improvement systems in a production environment.
* Strong understanding of pipe fabrication, welding, structural fabrication, production planning, material control, quality systems, and shop operations.
* Ability to build capacity plans, interpret production data, identify constraints, and translate performance information into corrective action.
* Experience coordinating with Estimating, Engineering, VDC, Procurement, Project Management, Quality, Safety, suppliers, and field teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organizational, financial, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple facilities and competing priorities.

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* Lean Six Sigma certification or equivalent formal training in Lean manufacturing and continuous improvement.
* Experience with ASME, AWS, weld-quality programs, fabrication codes, and customer-specific quality requirements.
* Experience with production-planning, ERP, manufacturing execution, scheduling, and performance-dashboard systems.
* Working knowledge of fabrication and detailing platforms such as Stratus, Tekla, SpoolFab, or comparable systems.
* Experience establishing or expanding multi-facility prefabrication and manufacturing operations.

records.title: Director, MSAT/External Manufacturing Management
records.description:
OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. We build buses, integrated satellites, and turnkey missions for customers to thrive in VLEO, below 300 km, where proximity compounds performance and drag self-cleans debris.

As part of the first 100 employees at Albedo, you will have a big impact on Albedo's trajectory to proliferating VLEO — whether you're advancing hardware to increase satellite longevity, scaling production for large constellations, building next-gen flight and ground software to push performance, or enabling missions that matter for national security and our day-to-day life here on Earth.

**How We Operate:** Albedo takes a first-principles approach — in space and in business. We move with speed, take calculated risks, and learn quickly. We use AI regularly to create leverage in every discipline across the company. We work in-person at our Broomfield, CO HQ to maximize team and company productivity. We work hard and with urgency to compound our first-mover advantage.

**Who We're Looking For:** Builders who want to own outcomes, not tasks. Systems thinkers who balance precision with iteration while thinking about the big picture. Individuals who are energized by creating a category rather than competing in an existing one. You'll join a team that has already proven what others said wasn't feasible and is now scaling and upgrading our VLEO buses & payloads to serve mission sets across sensing, communications, and responsive operations.

If you can feel the excitement running through your veins, apply to be one of the Bedo 100.

### **What You'll Do:**

* Own Albedo's production operations across Supply Chain, Assembly, Integration & Test (AI&T), and Facilities, ensuring flight hardware is delivered on schedule, within budget, and to quality requirements.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary team of engineers, technicians, test personnel, and supply chain professionals, including hiring, performance management, and workforce planning.
* Develop and execute integrated production plans, aligning material readiness, build schedules, staffing, and test capacity across vehicle and subsystem builds.
* Set supply chain strategy and priorities, ensuring sourcing, supplier development, procurement, and long-lead planning stay ahead of production demand.
* Oversee AI&T execution from assembly through integration, functional and environmental testing, and delivery. Drive improvements in processes, tooling, and test infrastructure.
* Lead facilities and production infrastructure planning, including buildout, commissioning, equipment, capacity expansion, and EHS.
* Establish and track operational metrics, including supplier delivery, material readiness, schedule adherence, labor efficiency, throughput, and first-pass yield.
* Partner with Engineering, Quality, Program Management, and Finance to transition designs into production, resolve risks, and align resources and priorities.
* Identify and prioritize improvements to production processes, tooling, and systems, balancing cost, schedule, and scalability.
* Lead major operational initiatives, including production rate increases, facility stand-up, and ERP/MES implementations.
* Remove roadblocks, support hands-on problem-solving, and champion a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

### **Your Ideal Skills and Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 8–12+ years of experience in aerospace or complex hardware manufacturing, spanning production, AI&T, and supply chain, with 5+ years leading technical teams.
* Proven ability to build and manage multidisciplinary teams, including hiring, workforce planning, performance management, and employee development.
* Strong understanding of spacecraft or similarly complex hardware assembly, integration, and test, including mechanical, electrical, functional, and environmental testing.
* Working knowledge of demand planning, MRP, strategic sourcing, supplier management, and long-lead procurement.
* Experience scaling manufacturing operations and facilities, including equipment, tooling, capacity planning, and EHS.
* Ability to balance cost, schedule, quality, and technical risk while identifying constraints and driving operational improvements.
* Experience managing operational KPIs, with familiarity in ERP/MRP, MES, QMS, configuration management, and aerospace workmanship standards.
* Strong leadership and communication skills, with a hands-on, solutions-oriented approach suited to a fast-paced startup environment.

### **Salary Range:**

* $168,197 - $190,000 per year

#### **Compensation and Benefits for Full-Time Roles:**

* + Employee friendly equity compensation
  + 4% direct matching 401k
  + Health Insurance: 100% employee coverage & 75% dependent coverage
  + Parental leave and childcare coverage
  + Flexible vacation and sick time from day one
  + 12 company holidays

  + Relocation package if not based in Denver

The **Senior Manager of Quality** will be responsible for leading all aspects of Quality Assurance throughout the product development lifecycle for L3Harris’ Culpeper, VA site. records.description:
Backed by more than a century of engineering excellence in thermal management technology, Modexus Solutions has sharpened its focus as a specialized leader in commercial HVAC and data center solutions into a new era. Throughout this evolution, our dynamic and collaborative culture, driven by our talented people, has propelled us to the forefront of the industry on a new frontier. At Modexus Solutions, we foster an environment of entrepreneurship and ingenuity, empowering our team to continually drive innovation. Joining Modexus Solutions means unlocking meaningful career growth, continuous development, and high-impact opportunities.

The answer is clear: your next opportunity starts here. Transform the future with us.

For more information about Modexus Solutions, visit www.modexussolutions.com

**Position Description**
------------------------

This role represents a critical executive leadership opportunity for a dynamic Director of Operations – Chillers to join the Global Operations team. Reporting directly to the VP of Global Operations with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President & General Manager (VPGM) of the Chillers business unit, this leader has direct operational responsibility for all global chiller manufacturing plants.

Each global chiller facility holds full SQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) execution accountability. To drive self-sufficient, world-class execution at the plant level, the Director of Operations – Chillers will lead a comprehensive, multi-functional organization where each plant team includes dedicated Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations resources.

As an integral member of the Global Operations team, this individual operates as an influential peer to Supply Chain (partnering to enable global Supply Chain and SIOP execution) and Materials (partnering to enable Materials management and Localized Procurement strategies), as well as the broader Global Operations leadership team. By bridging global functional capabilities with plant-level execution and business unit strategy, the Director of Operations – Chillers will drive rapid operational transformation, capacity expansion, and sustainable business growth.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **1. Global Plant Leadership & SQDC Execution Accountability**

* Hold direct operational oversight and P&L/conversion cost accountability for all global chiller manufacturing facilities.
* Drive rigorousSQDC (Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost) daily management and execution across every chiller site:

* **Safety:** Champion a zero-injury culture, ensuring proactive EHS compliance, ergonomic improvements, and behavioral safety leadership across all plants.
* **Quality:** Ensure zero-defect manufacturing standards, robust quality management systems, customer compliance, and rapid root-cause corrective actions.
* **Delivery:** Achieve industry-leading on-time delivery (OTD) and lead-time competitiveness through effective line balancing, capacity tracking, and constraint management.
* **Cost:** Optimize direct and indirect labor productivity, overhead absorption, scrap reduction, and continuous conversion cost improvements.

### **2. Multi-Functional Team Management & Talent Development**

* Lead, mentor, and develop Plant Managers and site leadership teams across the global chiller footprint.
* Ensure each plant's respective organization is effectively structured and resourced across Safety, Quality, Materials, and Manufacturing Operations to deliver autonomous day-to-day SQDC execution.
* Build organizational capability, establish clear succession plans, and foster an empowered, high-accountability, results-oriented culture across both salaried and direct labor workforces.

**Job Responsibilities Continued**
----------------------------------

**3. Matrixed & Peer Collaboration**

* **Business Unit Alignment (Dotted Line to VPGM of Chillers):** Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VPGM of Chillers, translating commercial growth strategies, customer requirements, and new product introductions (NPI) into scalable manufacturing execution plans.

records.description:
In this role, the Director of Program Operations leads a team of Operations Program Managers (OPM) and Material Program Managers (MPM) responsible for the operational elements of program execution within Mercury's PCC Manufacturing Center of Excellence. This role serves as a conduit between the line of business and operational teams, ensuring seamless coordination across engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, and growth functions.

You will be responsible for developing and executing operational program plans for critical programs, overall ownership of operational program performance, and internal communication of customer requirements affecting operational execution.

The Director of Program Operations will support proposals by providing accurate basis of cost estimates, focusing on supply chain material costs in addition to manufacturing labor costs. This work will be performed in conjunction with factory operations, supply chain, and engineering functions. Candidates must have excellent written and oral communications skills to influence across multiple functions and communicate effectively with external partners.

This role is on site at one of the following Mercury facilities: **Phoenix AZ**

**Job Responsibilities:**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of OPMs and MPMs accountable for operational aspects of program life cycle from proposal, development, production, sustainment, & delivery.
* Serve as the primary liaison between the line of business and operations, communicating customer requirements that affect manufacturing and supply chain execution.
* Responsible for meeting the financial objectives of the business unit, including the management of Estimate at Completion (EACs) specific to operations labor and material content.
* Oversee supply chain and manufacturing milestones to ensure compliance with contract baseline.
* Monitor program risks and opportunities, including obsolescence management, reporting, and improvement actions.
* Support and present operations metrics and data through program reviews (both internal and external) to Mercury and customer leadership.
* Champion efforts to meet readiness requirements throughout an NPI stage-gate process.
* Change leader, helping to drive Mercury's strategy, structure, and values.
* Strategic thinking coupled with ROI / business case development.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree.
* Typically requires 10+ years prior relevant experience in functional areas of Supply Chain, Operations (including Production Control), Program Management, or technical Project Management.
* Strong financial acumen with experience providing input into and reviewing EACs, along with development of business cases.
* Experience in review and understanding of Statements of Work (SOW) and project requirements (technical and commercial).
* Strong analytical skills, problem‑solving capabilities, and attention to detail.
* Experience developing and mentoring high‑performing teams.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. government issued security clearance is required. U.S. citizenship is required, as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* A self-starter, capable of achieving organizational and program objectives, and able to interface with all levels of internal management and external stakeholders.
* Ability to succeed in fast paced, developmental environment.
* Excellent time management skills and the ability to assign the appropriate priorities to the many tasks that need to be performed.
* Knowledge of US Government acquisition laws and regulations (FAR).
* Proficiency in ERP/MRP business systems.
* Knowledge of Mercury-type products with surface mount technology.
* Excellent communication skills (written, verbal, and presentation), leadership abilities, and the ability to work in an IPT environment.
