records.title: VP, Regional Manufacturing
records.description:
**Overview**

Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.

**Compensation:**
$185,048 - $248,596. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.

**Location:**
Dallas, TX

**Health Benefits**

Benefits of working for Primo Brands:

Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA)

**Retirement/Investing**

401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

**Insurance**

Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment

**Other Great Benefits**

Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.

**Responsibilities**

The Regional Vice President (RVP), Manufacturing is responsible for leading the end-to-end manufacturing operations across a multi-site regional network within Primo Brands. This executive leader drives safety, quality, production, cost, service, people, and continuous improvement performance across factories while ensuring alignment with enterprise Supply Chain strategies and business objectives.

The RVP, Manufacturing partners closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Procurement, Planning, HR, and Finance leaders to deliver operational excellence, optimize manufacturing capacity, develop organizational capability, and support long-term business growth. The role is accountable for creating a high-performance culture that prioritizes safety, quality, associate engagement, customer service, and productivity improvements.

The Regional Vice President, Manufacturing reports to the Senior Vice President, Manufacturing Operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Safety & Compliance Leadership**

* Lead a culture where safety is the first priority and operational decisions reflect a zero-harm mindset.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive accountability for safety performance, incident reduction, risk mitigation, and compliance excellence.
* Serve as a visible champion for workplace safety and associate well-being.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead manufacturing performance across multiple factories, ensuring consistent execution against operational objectives.
* Deliver production plans that support customer demand, service expectations, and inventory requirements.
* Drive schedule attainment, throughput, asset utilization, and manufacturing reliability.
* Optimize regional manufacturing capacity and network performance.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems and operational governance routines.

**Food Safety & Quality**

* Champion food safety and quality excellence across all facilities.
* Ensure manufacturing sites maintain compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company standards.
* Provide leadership oversight of quality management systems, audits, inspections, recalls, and corrective action processes.
* Promote a culture of first-time-right execution and continuous quality improvement.

**Financial & Productivity Performance**

* Own regional manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, conversion costs, and operating performance.
* Deliver annual productivity, cost savings, and efficiency targets.
* Identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve OEE, optimize labor deployment, and improve asset performance.
* Partner with Finance to ensure operational results support annual business plans and long-range objectives.

**Talent & Organizational Leadership**

* Build and lead high-performing teams through effective leadership, coaching, succession planning, and talent development.
* Develop strong Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Technical Managers, Operations Managers, and functional leaders.
* Drive leadership capability, workforce planning, succession readiness, and organizational effectiveness.
* Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and associate engagement.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead implementation of manufacturing excellence initiatives across the region.
* Drive improvements in OEE, asset reliability, labor productivity, quality, and service performance.
* Leverage Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustainable results.
* Establish performance metrics and governance processes that accelerate operational excellence.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Contribute to the development and execution of Supply Chain and Manufacturing strategies.
* Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate network optimization opportunities, capacity investments, automation initiatives, and capital projects.
* Lead manufacturing integration, transformation, and change management initiatives.
* Support enterprise growth through scalable operational solutions and disciplined execution.

**Scope of Responsibility**

* Multiple manufacturing facilities within assigned region.
* Direct leadership of Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Regional Engineering, Manufacturing Excellence, and operational support functions.
* Accountability for regional safety, quality, production, service, cost, talent, and financial performance.
* Significant influence on capital planning, organizational design, and operational strategy.

**Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business, or related field required.
* Master's Degree (MBA or related discipline) preferred.

**Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years leading multi-site manufacturing operations.
* Experience managing large-scale manufacturing networks in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or related industries.
* Proven success leading large teams through operational transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing significant P&L, productivity, and capital investment responsibilities.

**Skills & Competencies**

* Executive leadership and influence.
* Manufacturing operations expertise.
* Safety and quality systems leadership.
* Financial and operational acumen.
* Strategic thinking and execution.
* Change leadership and organizational transformation.
* Talent development and succession management.
* Data-driven decision making.
* Cross-functional collaboration.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

**Success Measures**

* Safety Performance
* Quality Compliance & Customer Metrics
* OEE and Asset Reliability
* Production Attainment
* Cost per Case Equivalent
* Labor Productivity
* Service Levels / OTIF
* Associate Engagement
* Leadership Bench Strength
* Productivity Savings Delivery
* Capital Project Execution
* Manufacturing Excellence Maturity

**If you're ready to embark on an exciting journey with Primo Brands, apply now!**

**Salary Range Disclaimer**

The salary range provided for this position is an approximation based on market research, internal compensation data and the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Final salary offers are determined through a comprehensive evaluation of candidate qualifications and may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location of the position. Other components of the compensation package, including benefits and bonuses, will also be considered. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we encourage open dialogue about compensation during the interview process.

Primo Brands’ established portfolio includes billion-dollar brands Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain® Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified brands, Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash® and AC+ION®. Our extensive direct-to-consumer offerings and industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases across Water Direct, Water Exchange, and Water Refill. At Primo Brands, our more than 11,000 associates are at the heart of what we do and deliver on our mission to provide healthy hydration to consumers wherever, however and whenever they want it. We believe in fostering a respectful culture, which values our associates who are deeply invested in quality hydration, our communities, and the sustainability of our packaging and water sources for generations to come.

Primo Brands is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.

Candidates must possess strong English language skills to effectively communicate with customers and provide exceptional service. Proficiency in English is essential for understanding customer needs, resolving inquiries, and collaborating with team members.

records.title: Plant Manager
records.description:
Job ID: 530933

Ash Grove is a CRH company with a legacy dating back to 1882. We combine technical expertise, safety and customer-focused solutions to deliver reliable performance for our customers. We manufacture and supply high-performance, advanced cementitious materials for the most demanding construction and infrastructure needs. With more than 2,000 people across 60 locations in the United States and Canada, we support a wide range of applications, from major infrastructure projects to the development and refurbishment of residential and non-residential buildings that support everyday life, from highways and bridges to schools and commercial buildings.

To learn more about us go to www.ashgrove.com

**Job Summary**

The Plant Manager plans, coordinates, and supervises the production operations, hazardous waste fuel program, maintenance activities, quality and safety programs, and other related functions involved in plant operations. This position incorporates directives provided by corporate management into policies and procedures to maintain standards and schedules. The position exercises direct or indirect supervision over a large number of employees.

**Job Location**

* This role will work out of our plant in Louisville, NE.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Promote and follow all plant safety guidelines.
* Conducts meetings with plant staff personnel to communicate, coordinate and discuss plant operations.
* Monitors, inspects, and reviews all plant activities.
* Ensures production schedule corresponds with sales forecasts.
* Assists in investigating customer and quality problems and concerns.
* Meets with government agencies and community groups concerning plant activities to ensure compliance with environmental regulations, policies, and standards.
* Prepares regular reports regarding plant production operations.
* Attends Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) training for waste-derived fuel activities.
* Promotes effective job performance through motivation, goals, and providing feedback.
* Promotes the safety program, compliance with safety standards, and participates in safety meetings.
* Establishes plant standards, short-term goals, and long-term strategic plans for production, maintenance, and improvements.
* Discusses new products, equipment, and ideas with staff and vendors.
* Analyzes plant costs and explore methods to improve productivity cost-effectively.
* Uses technology to develop a continuous improvement plan for the plant.
* Troubleshoots various problems and performance barriers.

**Job Requirements**

* Ability to read, write, and understand warning labels, instructions, signs, etc.
* Minimum 4 Year - Bachelors Degree in engineering, chemistry, natural sciences, business administration, or closely related field.
* Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
* Ability to develop and deliver effective presentations
* Ability to make decisions and solve problems with high attention to detail and accuracy
* Ability to make sound independent judgments regularly
* Ability to effectively coach and deliver constructive feedback
* Ability to inspire and develop staff
* Proficient in effective negotiation skills in business and construction contracts
* Proficient in Microsoft Office365
* Ability to effectively use computers for general word processing, spreadsheets, presentations, e-mail, internet, and customized company programs.
* Ability to communicate the company's vision into actionable goals and contributions for plant personnel.
* Ability to network with industry professionals, consultants, vendors, suppliers, regulators, and the community.
* Knowledge of safety and environmental health regulations.
* Knowledge of cement chemistry, physical testing, and concrete performance.
* Knowledge of various systems for cement manufacturing (crushing, grinding, pyro processing, chemistry).
* Ability to work from general policies and procedures.
* Ability to refer to supervisor when clarification or interpretation of the organizational policy

**What CRH Offers You**

* Highly competitive base pay
* Comprehensive medical, dental and disability benefits programs
* Group retirement savings program
* Health and wellness programs
* An inclusive culture that values opportunity for growth, development, and internal promotion

**About CRH**

CRH has a long and proud heritage. We are a collection of hundreds of family businesses, regional companies and large enterprises that together form the CRH family. CRH operates in a decentralized, diversified structure that allows you to work in a small company environment while having the career opportunities of a large international organization.

If you’re up for a rewarding challenge, we invite you to take the first step and apply today! Once you click apply now, you will be brought to our official employment application. Please complete your online profile and it will be sent to the hiring manager. Our system allows you to view and track your status 24 hours a day. Thank you for your interest!

Ash Grove Cement, a CRH Company, is an Affirmative Action and Equal Opportunity Employer.

EOE/Vet/Disability

CRH is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, status as a protected veteran or any other characteristic protected under applicable federal, state, or local law.

AI tools may be used in certain stages of the employment lifecycle, such as candidate review; however, all final employment decisions will be made by a person.

records.description:
LHH is seeking a Plant Manager for a Direct Hire, Permanent Placement position with a manufacturing client located near Fort Wayne, IN. This is an opportunity to lead a growing manufacturing operation where you will have significant autonomy and direct influence over business and operational performance. You will join an existing team, provide guidance, drive business growth, and lead critical projects with key customers. The compensation is commensurate to experience and will range between $140,000–165,000 per year plus bonus and includes comprehensive benefit and insurance plans, generous Paid Time Off, and a 401K plan with a company match.

***\*\*\*Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship.\*\*\****

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Provide overall leadership and direction for across the manufacturing facility.
* Build an engaged, accountable culture through visible leadership, open communication, coaching, and employee development.
* Evaluate production performance and operating data to identify opportunities for efficiency, capacity, and cost improvements.
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase productivity, reduce waste, and deliver measurable financial results.
* Manage staffing, training, labor utilization, production schedules, and resources to support changing business requirements.
* Review and improve operating procedures, standard work, and processes to strengthen consistency and accountability.
* Develop operating budgets and manage plant spending with a strong focus on profitability and cost control.
* Lead strategic planning activities and establish performance measures that support key organizational objectives.
* Direct capital investments and special projects from planning through implementation and performance validation.
* Improve equipment reliability, utilization, manufacturing capacity, and overall operational effectiveness.
* Maintain strong customer service while balancing production priorities, operating costs, and delivery expectations.
* Foster collaboration across departments and effectively lead employees with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and personalities.
* Maintain a strong safety culture and ensure operations comply with applicable workplace and regulatory requirements.
* Proactively identify operational risks, develop practical action plans, and follow initiatives through completion.
* Partner with technical and business leaders to support long-term growth and continuous operational improvement.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* **Bachelor Degree in Engineering, Business Management, Operations, or related field is preferred**
* **Minimum of 10+ years of leadership experience within a manufacturing facility is required**
* **Must have at least 5+ years of experience at the Plant Manager level**
* **Must have the ability to manage P&L, labor costs, scheduling, capacity, and capital expenditures**
* Must have experience with ERP/MRP systems and data-driven operational reporting
* Ideal candidates will have experience with Lean Manufacturing
* Strong communication, analytical, problem-solving, and cross-functional leadership skills.
* **Must be authorized to work in the U.S. without employer sponsorship.**

If you or someone in your network fit this profile and would like to apply for this Plant Manager position near Fort Wayne, IN then please submit your application alongside your resume using the link in this posting.

**Equal Opportunity Employer/Veterans/Disabled**

To read our Candidate Privacy Information Statement, which explains how we will use your information, please navigate to https://www.lhh.com/us/en/candidate-privacy

The Company will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records in accordance with federal, state, and local laws and/or security clearance requirements, including, as applicable:

* The California Fair Chance Act
* Los Angeles City Fair Chance Ordinance
* Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers
* San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance

records.description:
With over 100 years of experience, Sika is a worldwide innovation and sustainability leader in the development and production of systems and products for commercial and residential construction, as well as the marine, automotive, and renewable energy manufacturing industries.

Sika is a specialty chemicals company with a globally leading position in the development and production of systems and products for bonding, sealing, damping, reinforcing, and protection in the building sector and industry. Sika has subsidiaries in 103 countries around the world, produces in over 400 factories and develops innovative technologies for customers worldwide. In doing so, it plays a crucial role in enabling the transformation of the consruction and transportation industries toward greater environmental compatibility. Approximately 33,000 employees generated CHF 11.20 billion in sales in 2025.

**Job Description**

The Plant Manager is responsible for leading the safe, efficient, compliant, and environmentally responsible operation and continued development of the Versailles facility. This role provides overall site leadership for manufacturing performance, including safety, quality, service, productivity, cost, people development, and continuous improvement. The incumbent will create a culture of accountability, trust, employee engagement, and operational excellence while representing the Corporation’s vision and values at the plant level.

***Specific Responsibilities:***

* Lead the plant safety culture by actively advancing Sika SAFE principles, ensuring compliance with safety rules and procedures, and driving progress toward annual safety objectives.
* Deliver annual quality, service, and productivity goals by ensuring strong manufacturing execution, disciplined problem solving, process control, and effective response to customer and business requirements.
* Build and sustain high-performing teams across production, maintenance, engineering, quality, materials, logistics, and support functions.
* Partner with engineering, maintenance, EHS, quality, supply chain, R&D, and commercial teams to support reliable operations, new product introductions, capital planning, preventive maintenance, and long-term site development.
* Drive continuous improvement using lean manufacturing, statistical process control, error-proofing, root cause analysis, standard work, and other structured problem-solving methods.
* Develop a flexible and capable organization that can respond effectively to changing customer demand, business priorities, product mix, and capacity requirements.
* Manage annual operating expense targets and execute approved capital projects to deliver committed safety, quality, capacity, cost, and productivity benefits.
* Ensure compliance with applicable federal, state, local, corporate, environmental, safety, and quality requirements.
* Select, coach, train, and develop salaried and hourly associates to strengthen capability, succession depth, accountability, and employee engagement.
* Communicate effectively across all levels of the organization and promote a culture of respect, teamwork, ownership, and continuous improvement.

**Qualifications**

•Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, or a related field preferred; MBA or advanced technical degree desirable.

•Minimum of 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including experience leading production teams and managing plant-level performance.

•Proven ability to lead safe, efficient, customer-focused manufacturing operations while improving quality, productivity, delivery, and cost performance.

•Strong knowledge of lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, root cause analysis, process control, preventive maintenance, and capital project execution.

•Demonstrated leadership capability with the ability to build trust, develop talent, set clear expectations, and hold teams accountable in a fair and consistent manner.

•Excellent communication skills, characterized by clarity, sincerity, sound judgment, and the ability to influence across hourly, salaried, functional, and senior leadership groups.

•Strong interpersonal skills with a leadership style grounded in respect, humility, collaboration, accountability, and employee engagement.

•Goal-oriented, well organized, and able to operate effectively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment with changing priorities.

•Working knowledge of Microsoft Office applications and the ability to use data, reports, and operating metrics to manage performance and drive improvement.

**Additional Information**

**Perks & Benefits**

* 401k with Generous Company Match
* Medical, Dental, and Vision Benefits
* Paid Parental Leave

* Life Insurance

* Disability Insurance

* Paid time off, Paid holidays

* Floating holidays + Paid Volunteer Time

* Wellness/Fitness Reimbursements

Want to learn more about this role and Jobot? Click our Jobot logo and follow
 
our LinkedIn page!
 
 
 
Job details:
 
**Strong engineering leader needed with extensive PCB & SMT experience / Relocation assistance available**
This Jobot Job is hosted by: Christine McNamara
 
Are you a fit? Easy Apply now by clicking the "Easy Apply" button
 
and sending us your resume.
 
Salary: $160,000 - $180,000 per year
 
 
 
**A bit about us:**
We are seeking a hands-on Engineering Operations Leader to drive performance, efficiency, and team development within a fast-paced SMT / PCB manufacturing environment. This role will lead engineering and operations initiatives focused on continuous improvement, process optimization, and operational excellence, while developing and scaling a high-performing technical team.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings a strong Lean Manufacturing mindset, deep experience in electronics contract manufacturing (SMT/PCB), and the ability to drive accountability and measurable results across the organization.
 
 
\*\*Relocation assistance available for those not local to the area
 
 
 
**Why join us?**
Medical, Dental, Vision coverage
 
401(k) with company match
 
Relocation assistance
 
Annual performance bonus
 
Generous PTO & sick leave
 
 
 
**Job Details**
Key Responsibilities:
 
 
Operations & Continuous Improvement
 

* Lead Lean Manufacturing initiatives to improve throughput, yield, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Identify and drive process improvements across SMT lines, PCB assembly, and supporting operations
* Implement and sustain Lean tools (Kaizen, 5S, value stream mapping, standard work, etc.)
* Analyze production data to identify inefficiencies and drive corrective actions
* Reduce scrap, rework, and downtime through structured problem-solving methodologies

Engineering Leadership
 

* Oversee engineering activities related to process development, troubleshooting, and optimization
* Partner with production to resolve complex technical and process challenges
* Support new product introductions (NPI) and ensure smooth transition into production
* Drive best practices across SMT processes including soldering, reflow, pick-and-place, inspection, etc.

Team Development & Leadership
 

* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers, technicians, and support staff
* Build a culture of accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement
* Establish clear KPIs and performance metrics for engineering and operations teams
* Identify skill gaps and implement training / development plans

Cross-Functional Collaboration
 

* Partner with quality, supply chain, and production leadership to align operational goals
* Drive collaboration between engineering and manufacturing teams to improve execution
* Support customer needs and ensure alignment with delivery and quality expectations

Qualifications:
 
 
Required:
 

* 7–10+ years of experience in electronics contract manufacturing (SMT / PCB environment required)
* Proven leadership experience managing and developing technical teams (engineering or maintenance)
* Strong background in Lean Manufacturing / Continuous Improvement
* Hands-on experience with SMT processes (pick-and-place, reflow, inspection, etc.)
* Demonstrated success driving operational efficiency, process improvements, and accountability
* ITAR eligibility required; experience working in an ITAR-regulated environment is a strong plus
* Individual must be a US Citizen due to ITAR regulations

Preferred:
 

* IPC certification (IPC-A-610, IPC-7711/7721, etc.)
* Experience with high-mix, low-volume or high-speed production environments
* Exposure to automation, process engineering, or advanced manufacturing technologies

Interested in hearing more? Easy Apply now by clicking the "Easy Apply" button.

We provide an inclusive work environment that celebrates diversity and all qualified candidates receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, age (40 and over), disability, military status, genetic information or any other basis protected by applicable federal, state, or local laws. Jobot also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories. It is Jobot’s policy to comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws respecting consideration of unemployment status in making hiring decisions.

Jobot will consider qualified candidates with criminal histories in a manner consistent with any applicable federal, state, or local law regarding criminal backgrounds, including but not limited to the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring and the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.

By applying for this job, you agree to receive calls, AI-generated calls, text messages, or emails from Jobot, and/or its agents and contracted partners. Frequency varies for text messages. Message and data rates may apply. Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages. You can reply STOP to cancel and HELP for help. records.title: Site Process & Manufacturing Engineering Director
records.description:
At Alstom, we build what millions depend on daily - rail transportation systems that can't afford to fail. We're more than 85,000 people worldwide creating the industry's most diverse portfolio: high-speed trains, metros, trams, maintenance services and integrated systems.

**More Than a Job: A Mission**

We seek a visionary leader to drive process and manufacturing excellence, designing and implementing advanced solutions that elevate operational performance. Join dedicated teams committed to transforming rail mobility, where your leadership shapes the future and leaves a lasting legacy.

**Your Role, Your Impact**

* Lead scalable process improvements to optimize manufacturing efficiency and support growth.
* Foster cross-functional collaboration between engineering, production, and quality teams.
* Ensure reliability and compliance in manufacturing operations through robust systems.
* Champion innovation by introducing new technologies and methodologies.
* Promote knowledge sharing and continuous improvement across the site.

You'll work with sharp, committed teams solving complex challenges that shape the future of mobility, ensuring seamless integration of business and technology.

**What You Bring**

* **Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering or related field**
 .
* **Extensive manufacturing (industrial) engineering experience (ideally minimum 8-10 years), including proven leadership responsibilities**
 .
* Experience in working with an ERP (such as SAP) for Bill of Materials, Routings, Configuration follow-up.
* Working knowledge of Quality and Health & Safety standards and systems.
* Expertise in lean manufacturing, process optimization, and industrial automation.
* Strong understanding of quality systems, regulatory standards, and operational excellence.
* Proven leadership, strategic thinking, and ability to inspire high-performing teams.

**How Success Is Measured**

* Achievement of delivery timelines and strategic manufacturing goals.
* Effective collaboration and leadership across multidisciplinary teams.
* Reduction in defects, increased efficiency, and proactive troubleshooting.

**Alstom, A Great Place to Grow**

* Work with cutting-edge technology and drive strategic vision.
* Make a global impact from our West Mifflin office.
* Advance your career through continuous learning and development.

Here, progress isn't always easy but the impact is real. Because the scale is massive, the tasks are complex when the system runs, the train moves, and the city connects that feeling stays with you. And the legacy lasts.

postedPay.title: Director, Sourcing and Production, Robert Graham (Menswear)

records.description:
**About Us**
Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the ha rd work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.
 
 
**Product Development**
From sourcing raw material s to manufacturing, order placement, pricing, quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production/product development team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results-driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.
 
 
**Specific Responsibilities Would Include**
The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines. The role primarily focuses on apparel development, with additional responsibility for trims and packaging across Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue Private Label.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and manage all aspects of the product development process, from concept and inspiration through quality assurance of finished goods to the end customer.
* Establish shared qualities and fabrics between Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue to ensure alignment across brands.
* Partner closely with overseas hubs and vendor teams to ensure understanding of departmental objectives and leverage vendor capabilities to drive initiatives that expand competencies as needed.
* Analyze product costs, identifying opportunities and collaborating cross-functionally to create solutions through product engineering that maximize product value while accounting for cost impact.
* Oversee cross-functional milestone performance; communicate risks, deadlines, and business impacts when deliverables are at risk.
* Lead vendor sourcing initiatives aligned with driving innovation and service within the overall sourcing strategy.
* Manage new vendor onboarding and ensure all internal partners are connected and prepared to support production needs.
* Facilitate vendor meetings to review in-season development, production, and delivery challenges, and drive solutions.
* Identify business risks and opportunities, escalate appropriately, and propose actionable recommendations for improvement.
* Collaborate closely with Design and Merchandising on product creation from concept to execution, utilizing budget and SKU plans.
* Create and maintain comprehensive material and product libraries with detailed product attributes and testing documentation.

**Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); advanced Adobe, Photoshop and Illustrator skills required
* SAP experience preferred
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills
* Strong team orientation and ability to work cross-functionally
* Ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High attention to detail and accuracy
* Knowledge of garment manufacturing, construction, and fabrication

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000
 
 
At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.
 
 
**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**
**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**
Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams .

The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines.

records.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.

**What You Will Experience In This Position**

The R&D NPI Engineering Senior Manager will be a strategic and hands-on leader who drives on-time delivery and best practices for our new product introduction (NPI) programs within our Data Solutions business. This role will lead, coach and mentor a team of project and program managers to ensure alignment with business goals through effective portfolio and process management. The manager will work closely with business unit leaders, product managers, and engineering leaders to drive and improve on-time delivery and cross-functional collaboration for our portfolio of NPI programs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Team Leadership & Development:**
Lead, mentor and inspire a high-performing, global project management team specializing in NPI Program execution. Develop a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and empower the team to drive excellence in project delivery.

**NPI Execution and Delivery:**
Oversee end-to-end execution of projects, ensuring on-time delivery, within scope and on budget while maintaining high quality outcomes.

**Cross-Functional Coordination:**
Partner closely with engineering, product management, integrated supply chain, manufacturing and operations teams to ensure alignment of project priorities, resources, and timelines, facilitating seamless execution of programs.

**Resource Allocation:**
Optimize resource planning and allocation across projects, balancing capacity dynamically to meet changing business priorities and ensure effective utilization

**Portfolio Management:**
Collaborate with key partners to drive the selection and prioritization of NPI projects, connected to our strategic objectives and business goals.

**Continuous Improvement**
: Own and evolve the NPI phase-gate process to ensure consistent and efficient product development lifecycle execution. Drive continuous evaluation and enhancement of our project management processes, tools and methodologies to improve efficiency and scalability of programs.

**Performance & Reporting:**
Define and track KPIs to measure project health and business impact. Lead monthly business reviews to communicate progress, risks, and opportunities to senior leadership.

**You Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering
* Ideally 10+ years of proven experience in NPI or PMO leadership roles, preferably in data or technology-driven environments of which 2+ years of people leadership experience, including coaching, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams
* Proven record of leading large-scale, complex projects and driving successful product introductions
* Proficiency in demonstrating expertise in PMO practices, methodologies, tools and processes.
* Outstanding ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams and drive results in a matrixed organization.
* Excellent communication, coaching, and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong analytical, problem solving and decision-making abilities to drive efficiency and optimize project outcomes.
* Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or engineering focused organizations

**We Have**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day
* nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
* Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.
* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work
* We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
* Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

* Innovative & adaptable
* Dedicated to absolute integrity
* Focused on the customer first
* Respectful and team oriented
* Optimistic and energizing
* Accountable for performance
* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency**

nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.

**Compensation Range**

$123,500.00 - $229,500.00

Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.

**Benefit Overview**

At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being. We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:

* Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.
* A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.
* Other supplemental benefits may include tuition reimbursement, caregiver, personal and parental leave, back-up care services, paid time off including volunteer time, a well-being program, and/or legal & identity theft protection.

At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.

records.description:
Work Model: This role can be performed remotely from an approved location, with flexibility based on business needs and applicable requirements.
 
 
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
 
 
Reporting to the Vice President, Regal Rexnord Business System (RBS) for the Automation and Motion Control (AMC) Segment, the Continuous Improvement (RBS) Director for the AMC Segment serves as the strategic leader responsible for accelerating operational excellence and driving sustainable business performance improvements across assigned manufacturing sites. This role partners closely with site leadership teams to deploy CI (RBS) principles, develop leadership capabilities, improve operational metrics, and create a culture of continuous improvement.
 
 
The Director, RBS acts as both coach and change agent, ensuring that RBS tools and behaviors become integrated into daily management systems and leadership practices. Success in this role is measured by measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth, employee engagement, and overall business results.
 
 
The role is accountable for translating AMC strategic objectives into clear RBS roadmaps, prioritizing initiatives with the highest business impact, and ensuring disciplined execution through leaders, site teams, and RBS/CI talent. The Director, RBS will regularly communicate progress, risks, and business impact to segment and division leadership and will influence stakeholders outside of the direct function to align priorities, resources, and decisions.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
This Role Will Make an Immediate Impact By:
 
 

* Partner with site leadership teams to align operational strategies with division and enterprise objectives.
* Facilitate the development and execution of annual and multi-year operational strategies.
* Lead deployment of the Regal Business System across assigned facilities.
* Ensure site improvement priorities support commercial growth, profitability, customer service, and capacity requirements.
* Drive accountability for achievement of business objectives and key performance indicators.
* Drive a culture where performance gaps are addressed through structured problem solving.
* Partnering with division and segment leadership to prioritize improvement initiatives, recommend resource plans, and support staffing and talent decisions within the RBS/CI organization.

**Other Key Responsibilities Include**

* Assess site maturity and develop roadmaps to advance RBS capabilities.
* Standardize the use of RBS tools and systems across sites.
* Conduct regular RBS assessments, audits, and gemba reviews.
* Ensure sustainability of improvements through standard work and leader accountability.
* Coach site leaders on RBS principles, lean leadership, and continuous improvement behaviors.
* Develop leadership capability in daily management, problem solving, visual management, and accountability systems.
* Facilitate workshops, training sessions, and leadership development activities at sites.
* Build organizational capability to achieve self-sustaining continuous improvement.
* Establish and improve visual management systems throughout manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and support functions.
* Drive implementation and effectiveness of tiered accountability processes.
* Ensure performance measures are visible, actionable, and aligned to business objectives.
* Improve management routines to accelerate issue identification and resolution.
* Develop problem-solving capabilities at all levels of the organization.
* Facilitate Kaizen events, Rapid Improvement Events, and cross-functional improvement projects.
* Coach teams in root cause analysis methodologies including A3, 5 Whys, Fishbone, and PDCA.
* Ensure countermeasures are implemented, verified, and sustained.

**Required Skills & Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, marketing, operations, supply chain, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
* 10+ years of continuous improvement, manufacturing or operations experience. Experience leading Lean/RBS transformation and maturity improvement across multiple sites, divisions, or business functions.
* Proven application of multiple CI tools, including 80/20, value stream mapping, 6S, flow, standard work, visual management, and structured problem solving.
* Black Belt in Lean/Continuous Improvement preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others, influence senior leaders, and align cross-functional stakeholders around strategic improvement priorities.
* Experience developing CI/RBS talent, coaching leaders, and building organizational capability through formal training, Gemba coaching, and leader standard work.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with plant teams, peers, executives, and external stakeholders as needed.
* Ability to travel up to 75% of the time to support assigned plants and divisions, regionally and internationally.

**Preferred Skills & Qualifications**

* MBA Preferred
* Lean deployment experience within a large, global, decentralized manufacturing environment.
* Industrial manufacturing industry experience.
* Knowledge of enterprise-wide business system tools or and continuous improvement frameworks.
* Experience in engineer-to-order or configure-to-order business environments.
* Experience improving transactional process areas such as customer care, engineering, finance, commercial, product management, or quote-to-cash.

**Pay Transparency**
Expected Base Salary Range: $132,000 – $205,600
 
 
The salary range provided is intended to display the value of the company's base pay compensation for this position. Salary is dependent on a multitude of factors, including but not limited to the physical worksite location, the geographic market of that location, candidate's skill set, level of experience, education and internal peer compensation comparisons among other potential factors.
 
 
**Export Controlled ITAR/EAR Compliance (Location & Position Dependent)**
Restrictions imposed by federal export control laws may limit this job opportunity to candidates who are a ‘U.S. Person’, which includes U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted asylum in the United States, and refugees in the United States, or who otherwise can qualify for a license that permits them to hold the position.
 
 
**Sponsorship**
Candidates must be eligible to work in the United States without requiring company sponsorship to obtain or keep U.S. work authorization.
 
 
**Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescription Drug Coverage
* Spending accounts (HSA, Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA)
* Paid Time Off and Holidays
* 401k Retirement Plan with Matching Employer Contributions
* Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance
* Paid Leaves
* Tuition Assistance

**About Regal Rexnord**
Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.
 
 
The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.
 
 
Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. Regal Rexnord has offices and manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. For more information, including a copy of our Sustainability Report, visit RegalRexnord.com.
 
 
**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**
Regal Rexnord is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex/gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, age, ancestry, national origin, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status (unless required by the applicable law or government contract), disability or protected veteran status or any other status or characteristic protected by law. Regal Rexnord is committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse and inclusive backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. If you’d like to view a copy of the company’s affirmative action plan for protected veterans/individuals with disabilities or policy statement, please email Recruiting@RegalRexnord.com. If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please e-mail Recruiting@RegalRexnord.com.
 
 
Equal Employment Opportunity Posters
 
 
**Notification to Agencies**
: Please note that Regal Rexnord Corporation and its affiliates and subsidiaries ("Regal Rexnord") do not accept unsolicited resumes or calls from third-party recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Master Service Agreement or similar contract and approval from HR to submit resumes for a specific requisition, Regal Rexnord will not consider or approve payment to any third-parties for hires made.

records.description:
**Director, Manufacturing Value Stream**
Global Value Stream As a Director on the Global Value Stream team, you will
*lead*
our Manufacturing value stream within HelloFresh's global supply chain, shaping the strategy and execution model for how we standardize, improve, and scale our operations worldwide. You will lead a team, set the department's operational agenda, and serve as a senior voice of operations across the organization. This is a high-impact leadership role that sits at the intersection of operations, technology, and global strategy.
 
 
***You will...***

* Define and execute the strategic direction for the portfolio of Manufacturing processes, owning the multi-year capability roadmap and global template.
* Lead and build a high-performing, accountable department with clear OKRs aligned to company strategy.
* Set the governance framework and operating model for how the Global Value Stream team designs, validates, and deploys process and technology standards internationally.
* Partner at the executive level with Operations, Product, Engineering, and others to align on global priorities, technology investments, and performance benchmarks.
* Serve as the final decision authority on process deviation requests, capability exceptions, and cross-market design trade-offs.
* Drive the organization's approach to continuous improvement, value stream analysis, and waste elimination at scale — setting the standard for how the company approaches process maturity.
* Ensure the team functions as an effective internal consultancy — providing rigorous expert support to regional operations, quality teams, and technology partners.

***You have...***

* 12–15+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, operations, or manufacturing — including significant senior leadership experience.
* Demonstrated success leading multi-functional teams across multiple geographies, with full accountability for operational outcomes.
* Deep expertise across multiple supply chain functional domains, with a breadth of experience that enables credible leadership across the full Value Stream portfolio.
* Strong commercial acumen and experience managing department budgets and delivering measurable business impact.
* Extensive experience with global process standardization, operational technology ecosystems (WMS/WES/WCS/automation), and large-scale transformation programs.
* A track record of developing senior talent and building high-performance organizations.
* Experience operating as a senior stakeholder in cross-functional governance and product/technology lifecycle processes.
* Ability to travel up to 25%

***You are...***

* A bold, strategic leader with the operational depth to earn the trust of both warehouse teams and the C-suite.
* Comfortable navigating ambiguity at the department level while maintaining clarity and pace for your team.
* A talent multiplier — known for developing strong leaders and creating organizations that outlast any individual.
* A rigorous, data-driven decision maker who moves fast without sacrificing quality or thoroughness.
* Passionate about building world-class operations at scale — energized by the complexity and impact of a global mandate.
* An outstanding communicator and influencer who can drive alignment across diverse cultures, functions, and levels of seniority.

**Additionally With This Role, You Will Have....**

* The opportunity to shape global operations at a leading food technology company with significant reach and impact.
* A high-ownership, low-bureaucracy environment where your work is visible and your decisions matter.
* Flexible working arrangements to support your work-life balance.
* Continuous development through HelloFresh Academies and access to internal mobility across 18 countries.
* An egoless, collaborative culture focused on learning, growth, and building something exceptional together.

***You’ll get…***

* Competitive salary, 401k with company match that vests immediately upon participation
* Generous PTO, including sabbatical, and parental leave of up to 16 weeks
* Comprehensive health and wellness benefits with options at $0 monthly, effective first day of employment
* Tuition reimbursement for continuing education (upon 2 years of service)
* Up to 85% discount on subscriptions to HelloFresh meal plans (HelloFresh, Green Chef, Everyplate, and Factor\_)
* Access to Employee Resource Groups that are open to all employees, including those pertaining to BIPOC, women, veterans, parents, and LGBTQ+
* Inclusive, collaborative, and dynamic work environment within a fast-paced, mission-driven company that is disrupting the traditional food supply chain

This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the responsibilities. However, the Company reserves the right to adjust, modify, or reassign work tasks and responsibilities as needed to meet changing business needs, operational requirements, or other factors.
 
 
**FOR CO POSTINGS**
*Our company is committed to fair hiring practices and complies with all applicable laws, including the Colorado Job Application Fairness Act (JAFA). In accordance with JAFA, we will not request your age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution on your initial application for employment.*
**Education**
*When submitting supporting documents such as a resume, curriculum vitae (CV), or educational transcripts, you may voluntarily redact or omit any information that would identify your age. This includes:*

* Dates of birth
* Dates of attendance at educational institutions
* Dates of graduation

*Your decision to redact this information will not adversely affect the consideration of your application. We evaluate all candidates based on their skills, qualifications, and experience. Please be aware that should you receive a conditional offer of employment, we may be required to request this information for legally permissible purposes, such as verifying eligibility for employment or for benefits administration and background checks.*

$148,050—$179,000 USD
 
 
Texas Pay Range
 
 
$143,850—$174,000 USD
 
 
Newark, NJ Pay Range
 
 
$164,850—$199,500 USD
 
 
Arizona Pay Range
 
 
$143,850—$174,000 USD
 
 
Illinois Pay Range
 
 
$148,050—$179,000 USD
 
 
This position is also eligible for the HelloFresh equity plan.

records.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering

postedPay.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering

records.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**Why This Role Exists**
------------------------

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Architect the system.** Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.
* **Build the digital backbone.** Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.
* **Fuse the sensors.** Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.
* **Automate where it pays.** Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.
* **Lead the three functions as one.** Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.
* **Own the applications engineering interface.** With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.
* **Industrialize the equipment.** Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.
* **Design for the factory.** Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.
* **Build quality in.** Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.
* **Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform.** Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.
* **Hire, develop, and retain.** Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
* 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.
* 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.
* Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.
* Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.
* Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.
* Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.
* Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.
* Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.
* Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.
* Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.
* In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.
* Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.
* AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).
* Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.
* Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

**Compensation**
----------------

For this role, the target salary range is $300,000 - $350,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. records.title: Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing

postedPay.title: Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing

records.description:
Rezolute is a pre-commercial ultra-rare disease company focused on significantly improving outcomes for individuals with hypoglycemia caused by hyperinsulinism (HI). Our fully human monoclonal antibody therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is designed to treat all forms of HI and has shown substantial benefit in clinical trials and real-world use for the treatment of congenital hyperinsulinism (cHI) and tumor hyperinsulinism (tHI).

**Position Summary**

Rezolute is seeking a proactive, execution-focused project management professional to coordinate external manufacturing programs as the company advances toward commercial manufacturing.

The Senior Manager, Project Management - External Manufacturing will manage integrated plans, communications, and deliverables across technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, and commercial readiness. Working with internal functional leads and contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs), this individual will align schedules, supplier commitments, and cross-functional dependencies with Rezolute’s Plan of Record (POR), supply requirements, and business priorities.

This role owns project coordination and follow-through, not technical oversight. External Manufacturing Operations, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance (QA), and designated functional experts retain responsibility for technical strategy, scientific assessments, manufacturing process decisions, and quality approvals.

### **Principal Duties and Responsibilities**

Integrated Project Planning and Execution

* Develop and maintain integrated project plans for external Drug Substance (DS) and Drug Product (DP) programs, defining scope, deliverables, owners, milestones, dependencies, and target dates.

* Align project baselines and supplier commitments with the POR, supply requirements, and approved priorities.

* Monitor critical-path activities and progress against plan; coordinate recovery actions for overdue or at-risk commitments with functional owners and suppliers.

* Assess scope, schedule, and resource changes with accountable stakeholders and route proposed changes through established approval processes.

Communications and Cross-Functional Coordination

* Serve as the project management point of contact between Rezolute teams and CDMOs, facilitating cross-functional coordination and timely communication of changes.

* Lead internal and supplier project meetings, using focused agendas to address progress, upcoming deliverables, dependencies, and decisions required.

* Maintain and distribute meeting records and action items with clear owners and due dates; drive follow-through to closure.

Workstream and Milestone Coordination

* Coordinate manufacturing and milestone readiness by tracking prerequisites, including material availability, documentation, internal reviews, and supplier deliverables.

* Integrate technical and quality review timelines into project schedules, including protocols, reports, and master or electronic batch records.

* Track schedule dependencies associated with change controls, deviations, investigations, and other quality-system activities in partnership with QA and technical owners.

* Coordinate handoffs from development and validation activities to routine commercial manufacturing, tracking agreed deliverables, receiving owners, and outstanding actions.

Risk, Issue, and Decision Management

* Maintain risk, issue, assumption, decision, and dependency logs, including accountable owners and required completion dates.

* Work with functional leads and suppliers to assess execution risks and track mitigation actions and residual risks.

* Facilitate issue resolution and escalate unresolved items or pending decisions, clearly communicating timing requirements and potential project impacts.

Reporting, Scope, and Project Controls

* Provide dashboards and leadership updates showing milestone performance, forecast completion dates, critical-path activities, risks, and decisions or intervention required.

* Partner with External Manufacturing leadership, Supplier Relationship Management (SRM), Business, and Procurement to define milestones, deliverables, assumptions, and timelines in supplier scopes of work.

* Support project-level financial tracking with budget owners, including planned work, supplier milestones, and the budget and schedule impacts of scope changes.

* Improve project management tools, reporting practices, and lessons-learned processes across the external manufacturing network.

### **Qualifications/Requirements:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific, engineering, business, project management, or related discipline.

* Minimum of seven years of relevant biopharmaceutical industry experience, including responsibility for managing cross-functional projects involving CDMOs or other external manufacturing partners.

* Demonstrated ability to manage integrated schedules, critical-path activities, risks, and changing priorities across multiple workstreams.

* Experience coordinating technology transfer, GMP manufacturing, process characterization, process validation, or commercial manufacturing readiness activities.

* Working knowledge of biopharmaceutical manufacturing and cGMP requirements sufficient to understand project dependencies and engage effectively with technical and quality teams.

* Strong meeting facilitation, written communication, and stakeholder management skills, including communication with external partners and senior leadership.

* Ability to translate technical discussions into clear project actions, decisions, and schedule implications while respecting functional decision-making authority.

* Strong organization, attention to detail, and follow-through, with the ability to drive accountability and prioritize independently in a matrixed environment.

* Proficiency in Smartsheet or comparable project management software and Microsoft Teams, Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

Preferred Qualifications:

* Experience supporting late-stage biologics programs transitioning to commercial manufacturing.

* Experience coordinating DS and/or DP manufacturing projects across multiple external partners.

* Experience working in a small to mid-sized biotechnology company.

* Experience tracking project budgets, supplier scopes of work, and change requests.

Core Competencies:

* Project Planning and Controls: Creates practical plans that connect workstreams and support timely delivery.

* Execution and Accountability: Establishes ownership and follows through on commitments.

* Communication and Collaboration: Builds productive relationships and keeps internal and external teams aligned.

* Risk and Issue Management: Anticipates challenges, coordinates mitigation, and escalates appropriately.

* Adaptability and Prioritization: Adjusts plans as circumstances change while maintaining focus on program objectives.

Rezolute (RZLT) currently anticipates the base salary for Senior Manager - Project Management External Manufacturing role could range from $165,000 to $180,000 and will depend, in part, on the successful candidate’s geographical location and their qualifications for the role, including education and experience. This position will also be eligible for an annual performance bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable plan (depending, in part, on company and individual performance and at the Company’s discretion on an individual basis). The compensation described above is subject to change and could be higher or lower than the range described based on current market survey data and the qualifications, education, experience and geographical location of the selected candidate.

Qualifying employees are eligible to participate in benefit programs such as:

* Health Insurance (Medical / Dental / Vision)

* Disability, Life & Long-Term Care Insurance

* Holiday Pay

* Tracking Free Vacation Program

* 401(k) Plan Match

* Educational Assistance Benefit

* Fitness Center Reimbursement

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against applicants due to race, ethnicity, gender, veteran status, or on the basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses and identifying potential inconsistencies or verification signals in application materials based on available information. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.
